info.description: Package admin is the operator's view of the fleet: orgs, users, roles, spend and system health.

get.summary: Is the fleet AI board: LLM generations over gen_ai spans (count, cost, avg/p95 latency, per-model), per-model usage from the live cloud_usage ledger, and the eval plane (traces, scores, score names, runs, and the average-score trend).
get.description:
Is the fleet AI board: LLM generations over gen_ai spans (count, cost,
avg/p95 latency, per-model), per-model usage from the live cloud_usage ledger, and
the eval plane (traces, scores, score names, runs, and the average-score trend).

Every signal degrades INDEPENDENTLY — a table that is absent or errors contributes its
zero value and the read still succeeds. Generation latency is a SEPARATE query from
generations and cost on purpose: a duration/attribute mismatch there must not zero
the two numbers that did read.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the lower time bound: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else reads as the
board's own default.

get.summary: Is the SaaS product-analytics board over the caller's tenant window: active customers, new and churned, retention, MRR, ARPU, the usage trend and the top customers by spend — every number folded from the commerce ledger, not sampled.
get.description:
Is the SaaS product-analytics board over the caller's tenant window: active
customers, new and churned, retention, MRR, ARPU, the usage trend and the top
customers by spend — every number folded from the commerce ledger, not sampled.

The window is the caller's, not the fleet's: a SuperAdmin gets every org, a
white-label admin only their own subtree (core.ScopedOrgs, the one scope predicate).

sources[] carries each upstream's freshness so a partial read is VISIBLE rather than
silently low: a ledger that answered for only some orgs marks commerce-ledger degraded
instead of publishing an undercount as healthy.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the lower time bound: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else reads as the
board's own default.

get.summary: Lists IAM applications for one owner org, forwarded VERBATIM from IAM's get-applications.
get.description:
Lists IAM applications for one owner org, forwarded VERBATIM from IAM's
get-applications. These are the platform's OIDC clients — the console reads clientId
off each row.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description:
Owner is the org whose rows to read. Defaults to the admin org, which owns the
platform's roles and applications.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description:
Page is the 1-based page number. Forwarded only when set — IAM applies its own
default otherwise.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: PageSize is rows per page. Forwarded only when set.

get.summary: Reads one chain of cloud's tamper-evident audit trail, newest first, with that chain's live integrity attached so a listing can be badged as verified.
get.description:
Reads one chain of cloud's tamper-evident audit trail, newest first, with
that chain's live integrity attached so a listing can be badged as verified.

When cloud has no local store configured it falls back to forwarding IAM's own
get-records trail verbatim — a DIFFERENT trail, federated so the endpoint never
regresses to an empty list. Those rows carry no integrity of ours, so the field is
null there.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org restricts the trail to one tenant.

parameters.name: sub
parameters.description: Sub restricts it to one actor (the validated subject that made the request).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Action restricts it to one action name, e.g. "admin.waitlist.grant".

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Resource restricts it to one resource kind, e.g. "credit-grant".

parameters.name: resourceId
parameters.description: ResourceID restricts it to one resource instance.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Result restricts it to "success" or "error".

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Since is the inclusive lower time bound, RFC3339. An unparseable value is
ignored rather than refused — one malformed filter must not hide the trail.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Until is the upper time bound, RFC3339, with the same tolerance.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: PageSize is rows per page, default 100.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Page is the 1-based page number, driving the offset.

get.summary: Walks EVERY hash chain this deployment keeps and reports each one: which chains were checked, how many records each holds, the head hash to pin externally against tail-truncation, and — when a chain is broken — the seq of the first bad record and why.
get.description:
Walks EVERY hash chain this deployment keeps and reports each one: which
chains were checked, how many records each holds, the head hash to pin externally
against tail-truncation, and — when a chain is broken — the seq of the first bad
record and why.

The trail is a FAMILY of chains, one per process, so the answer is a set and not a
boolean: `intact`, `broken` and `unread` count the three verdicts and sum to the
number of chains. A chain that could not be READ is reported `unread` and is never
a pass — an unreadable chain and a verified one must not render the same, which is
the whole reason this is not one flag.

An unconfigured store is an honest failure here rather than a fabricated pass.

get.summary: Lists the tenant Base instances in the caller's window — a SuperAdmin sees every tenant's, anyone else only their own subtree's.
get.description:
Lists the tenant Base instances in the caller's window — a SuperAdmin sees every
tenant's, anyone else only their own subtree's.

The scope is enforced TWICE: the upstream is asked for the caller's org, AND every row
it returns is re-checked against the resolved scope. An upstream that ignored the
filter therefore degrades to empty, never to a cross-tenant leak.

The Base engine is being embedded into cloud; until it lands this proxies
BASE_ADMIN_URL and, when that is unset, answers 200 with an empty list and msg saying
so — the honest not-yet state, never fabricated instances.

get.summary: Reads one org's usage caps: its spend alerts plus the derived period spend, over/warn state and reset time.
get.description:
Reads one org's usage caps: its spend alerts plus the derived period
spend, over/warn state and reset time.

These are the SAME rows the customer edits in their own console — a platform override
and a customer budget are one model, not two.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org is the tenant to act on. Required for a SuperAdmin — they must name their
target; ignored for a white-label admin, who always acts on their own org.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the cap to edit or remove, from the path. Unused by the list and create ops.

post.summary: Sets a usage cap on one org — a platform override of a customer budget, written to the customer's own spend-alert rows.
post.description:
Sets a usage cap on one org — a platform override of a customer budget,
written to the customer's own spend-alert rows. The body is commerce's spend-alert
contract, forwarded byte-for-byte.

delete.summary: Removes one cap by id, lifting the ceiling entirely.
delete.description: Removes one cap by id, lifting the ceiling entirely.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the cap to edit or remove, from the path. Unused by the list and create ops.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org is the tenant to act on. Required for a SuperAdmin — they must name their
target; ignored for a white-label admin, who always acts on their own org.

patch.summary: Edits one cap by id — raise or lower the ceiling, flip enforcement.
patch.description:
Edits one cap by id — raise or lower the ceiling, flip enforcement. The

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the cap to edit or remove, from the path. Unused by the list and create ops.

get.summary: Rolls the fleet's compute usage up to one row per (org, app, project, kind): how many distinct machines ran in the window, how many are still active, what they billed, and when each group last emitted an event.
get.description:
Rolls the fleet's compute usage up to one row per (org, app, project, kind):
how many distinct machines ran in the window, how many are still active, what they
billed, and when each group last emitted an event. The console folds these into its
org → app → project tree.

A machine counts as ACTIVE when its LATEST lifecycle event is not a terminal one
(stop/destroy/terminate/delete/off/shutdown/expire and their past tenses) — the same
fold the console applies, done in the warehouse so the count is over every machine and
not just the page.

Honest-empty when the warehouse is not connected or hanzo.compute_usage is not
provisioned yet: an empty list, never a fabricated fleet.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
Kind narrows to one workload class (bot | machine | cluster | nodepool |
container | function | …). An OPEN spectrum matched as a plain string, lowercased
to the warehouse's convention; empty means every kind.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org narrows to one tenant. Empty means every tenant — this board is
cross-tenant by nature.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Range is the lower time bound: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else reads as 30d.

get.summary: Lists every customer org at a glance, sorted by slug: owner email, plan, suspend status, member count, balance, month-to-date spend and MRR.
get.description:
Lists every customer org at a glance, sorted by slug: owner email, plan,
suspend status, member count, balance, month-to-date spend and MRR.

Each row costs one IAM read plus the org's money reads, fanned out under a fixed
concurrency ceiling so a large fleet cannot stampede the upstreams. Every read is
best-effort per row: an upstream miss degrades THAT field to its honest zero rather
than failing the fleet.

get.summary: Answers GET /v1/admin/customers/:org.
get.description: Answers GET /v1/admin/customers/:org.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the tenant slug from the path.

post.summary: Issues a staff credit grant to the org named in the path — a comp, refund or promo — through the ONE credit-write path core.ApplyGrant, which validates the amount against the per-grant cap, checks the org exists, moves the money and records the tamper-evident audit row.
post.description:
Issues a staff credit grant to the org named in the path — a comp, refund
or promo — through the ONE credit-write path core.ApplyGrant, which validates the
amount against the per-grant cap, checks the org exists, moves the money and records
the tamper-evident audit row.

The credit lands on the account account.Payer resolves, NOT necessarily the org: name
a member of a pooled org and the pool is credited. The receipt echoes the subject so
the caller can see which.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the tenant to credit. Required.

post.summary: Restores access for every member of the org, undoing a suspend.
post.description:
Restores access for every member of the org, undoing a suspend. It
reports the same per-user breakdown.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the tenant slug from the path.

post.summary: Cuts off every member of the org: IAM refuses a forbidden user at login AND at token issuance, so a suspended customer can neither sign in nor mint a fresh token.
post.description:
Cuts off every member of the org: IAM refuses a forbidden user at
login AND at token issuance, so a suspended customer can neither sign in nor mint a
fresh token. Fully reversible with ReactivateCustomer.

The result names every user updated and every user that was NOT — a partial failure
leaves the org in a mixed state and says so instead of reporting a clean success.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the tenant slug from the path.

get.summary: Answers GET /v1/admin/finance.
get.description:
Answers GET /v1/admin/finance. It reads the multi-vendor COGS from commerce
/v1/costs, the DO promo-credit/burn-down treasury view, and the fleet commerce revenue,
then hands them to ComputeFinance. SuperAdmin only.

post.summary: Carries ONE org's current commerce prepaid balance into the native finance wallet — the one-time cutover between the two ledgers.
post.description:
Carries ONE org's current commerce prepaid balance into the native finance
wallet — the one-time cutover between the two ledgers.

It is IDEMPOTENT: the deposit uses the fixed ref "backfill:<org>", so re-running it
credits the wallet at most once. Safe to retry.

The pre-migration balance is read from the CO-RESIDENT commerce ledger, not over HTTP:
the admin HTTP client dials an unroutable in-process address and would read $0, and a
phantom zero would silently carry nothing while reporting success. When commerce is
not co-resident this fails rather than migrating nothing.

get.summary: Reads the platform control-plane board: every runtime launch/release switch (waitlist, public signup, subsystem activation, gateway limits, network ids) with its LIVE value and where that value came from — a stored definition or the compiled-in default.
get.description:
Reads the platform control-plane board: every runtime launch/release
switch (waitlist, public signup, subsystem activation, gateway limits, network ids)
with its LIVE value and where that value came from — a stored definition or the
compiled-in default.

put.summary: Stores or overwrites ONE platform switch's definition and answers with the whole board as it now stands.
put.description:
Stores or overwrites ONE platform switch's definition and answers with the
whole board as it now stands. The flip is hot: this pod applies it immediately and
peers converge within one evaluation TTL (15s by default), with no redeploy.

The body reaches the flag engine BYTE-FOR-BYTE — it is the engine's definition
format, not this layer's, so a field the engine understands and admin does not must
still arrive intact. setFlagIn names the two fields that matter for documentation; it
is not a filter.

The write is recorded in the store's activity log against the caller's email.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the switch to write, taken from the path (e.g. "waitlist.chat").

get.summary: Reads the credit-grant ledger across ALL orgs, newest first — who granted what to whom, when, and from which money bucket.
get.description:
Reads the credit-grant ledger across ALL orgs, newest first — who granted what
to whom, when, and from which money bucket.

It is a PROJECTION of the tamper-evident audit trail, not a second store: every grant
is written there as action "admin.customer.credit", so this view cannot drift from
what actually happened, and FAILED grants appear too.

A deployment with no local audit store has no history to project, and says so with an
empty list and a msg rather than an error.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org filters by the ACTOR's org (the staff org that issued the grant), which is
rarely what a reader wants — the target org is a row field, not a filter.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description:
Result filters by outcome: "success" or "error". Empty returns both, which is
the point of this view — a refused grant is as interesting as a granted one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned. Default 200.

post.summary: Issues a credit grant to any org from the operator Grants view, with the target named in the body.
post.description:
Issues a credit grant to any org from the operator Grants view, with the
target named in the body. It funnels through the SAME core.ApplyGrant that
POST /v1/admin/customers/:org/credit uses, so there is exactly ONE credit-write path
and one audit trail behind both.

get.summary: Serves the whole DigitalOcean infrastructure board: droplets, volumes, DOKS clusters and load balancers, each cross-referenced against every cluster's live Kubernetes state so the board can say what is safe to destroy and what is not.
get.description:
Serves the whole DigitalOcean infrastructure board: droplets, volumes, DOKS
clusters and load balancers, each cross-referenced against every cluster's live
Kubernetes state so the board can say what is safe to destroy and what is not.

It is cached for up to a minute because one read is a fan-out over the DO API plus a
full pod/PV listing per cluster. Staleness is never load-bearing: every MUTATION
re-scans from scratch and ignores this cache.

Only an unusable DO account is a hard failure. A partial read still produces a board,
with the failing source named in sources[] — except for clusters and volumes, which
the safety verdict depends on; without those the analysis degrades rather than
classifying anything it cannot prove.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description:
Refresh, when present, forces a full re-scan instead of serving the cached
snapshot. Every MUTATION re-scans regardless — this is only for the reader.

post.summary: Sets a node pool's node count — the ONE correct way to change how many nodes a DOKS cluster has.
post.description:
Sets a node pool's node count — the ONE correct way to change how many
nodes a DOKS cluster has.

The response states what the board could NOT prove: DOKS picks which nodes a shrink
removes, so no particular pod is shown to survive one. See NodePool.ScaleTo.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DOKS cluster id, from the path.

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description:
Pool is the node pool, from the path. Its DO id or its name — both are unique
within a cluster, and an operator reads the name off the board.

delete.summary: Destroys a droplet the board has just proven is NOT a DOKS node.
delete.description:
Destroys a droplet the board has just proven is NOT a DOKS node. There
is no snapshot-first undo for a droplet the way there is for a volume: the local disk
goes with it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO droplet id, from the path. Numeric.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size is the target DigitalOcean size slug on resize, e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb".

parameters.name: disk
parameters.description:
Disk requests a PERMANENT resize that grows the disk. DO can never resize such a
droplet down again, so it defaults false — a CPU/RAM-only change, reversible.

post.description:
Changes a droplet's plan. Same refusal as delete and for the same
reason: a DOKS node's size is the node pool's to declare.

disk=true is a PERMANENT resize — the disk grows and DO can never resize the droplet
DOWN again. disk=false (the default) changes CPU/RAM only and is reversible. DO
requires the droplet to be powered off and applies the change asynchronously, so the
response carries the action to poll, not a completed change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO droplet id, from the path. Numeric.

delete.summary: Destroys a load balancer the board has just proven no live type=LoadBalancer Service in any cluster targets.
delete.description:
Destroys a load balancer the board has just proven no live
type=LoadBalancer Service in any cluster targets.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO load balancer id, from the path.

post.summary: Marks one cluster node unschedulable — or schedulable again — and can drain the pods already on it.
post.description:
Marks one cluster node unschedulable — or schedulable again — and can drain
the pods already on it.

It is the ONE infra change that does not go through the run discipline, because there
is no destructive verdict to check: cordoning is reversible and evicting respects the
cluster's own PodDisruptionBudgets. It reads the cached board for the same reason.
The outcome is audited either way, and the result reports how many pods were evicted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the node's droplet id, from the path.

delete.summary: Destroys a volume the board has just proven no PersistentVolume in any cluster references.
delete.description:
Destroys a volume the board has just proven no PersistentVolume in any
cluster references. Irreversible, so it snapshots first unless explicitly waived —
the snapshot IS the undo.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO volume id, from the path.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description:
Snapshot is the snapshot-first switch on DELETE. Anything other than the literal
"false" snapshots before destroying — the snapshot IS the undo, so waiving it is
deliberate and explicit.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
Name is the snapshot name on the snapshot action. Blank gets a deterministic
"<volume>-predelete-<unix>" so the undo is findable in the DO console.

parameters.name: sizeGiB
parameters.description:
SizeGiB is the target size on the resize action. A volume only ever grows —
ExpandTo is the verdict that refuses a shrink, so this is not validated here.

post.description:
Grows a volume. GROW ONLY — see Volume.ExpandTo for why the other
direction is a data migration this board deliberately refuses to run.

The MECHANISM follows the volume's owner, because there is exactly one way to grow each
kind completely. A volume a PVC claims is grown by patching the claim: the CSI driver
then resizes the DigitalOcean device AND grows the filesystem on it, leaving claim, PV,
device and filesystem all agreeing. Calling DigitalOcean directly for that volume would
grow the device while the PV kept declaring the old capacity and the filesystem never
grew at all. One operation, one correct mechanism per owner — not two ways to do it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO volume id, from the path.

post.summary: Takes a point-in-time snapshot of one volume — the undo a delete relies on, available on its own so an operator can take one before any risky change.
post.description:
Takes a point-in-time snapshot of one volume — the undo a delete relies
on, available on its own so an operator can take one before any risky change.

It re-scans the board first (never the cache) so the volume it snapshots is one that
exists right now, and audits the outcome either way.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DO volume id, from the path.

Answers with the validated operator identity — who the console is signed in as,
which tier they are, and how wide their tenant window is. The fields come from the

get.summary: Answers GET /v1/admin/metrics by aggregating commerce.events directly (fleet-wide, no per-org fan-out).
get.description:
Answers GET /v1/admin/metrics by aggregating commerce.events directly
(fleet-wide, no per-org fan-out). SuperAdmin only.

	GET /v1/admin/metrics?window=30d&limit=20

parameters.name: window

Window is the movement window the new/churned MRR and the recent feed are

parameters.name: limit

get.description: moneyBoardHandler answers GET /v1/admin/money.

get.summary: Is the fleet-wide observability board: LLM usage (requests, tokens, cost, errors, top orgs, top models), trace RED metrics (count, p50/p95/p99 latency in ms, error rate, top services), fleet log volume, and the O11yAI generation rollup — all aggregated across EVERY tenant, with no org filter applied.
get.description:
Is the fleet-wide observability board: LLM usage (requests, tokens, cost,
errors, top orgs, top models), trace RED metrics (count, p50/p95/p99 latency in ms,
error rate, top services), fleet log volume, and the O11yAI generation rollup — all
aggregated across EVERY tenant, with no org filter applied.

Every signal degrades INDEPENDENTLY. A table that is absent or errors contributes its
zero value and the read still succeeds, so the board renders exactly what the
warehouse holds rather than failing whole because one of four sources is missing.
Same when the warehouse is not connected at all: the zero board, never a fabricated
fleet.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the lower time bound: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else reads as the
board's own default.

get.summary: Lists the tenant directory one row per org, sorted by slug: member count and the org's month-to-date spend and credit balance, read live from IAM and commerce.
get.description:
Lists the tenant directory one row per org, sorted by slug: member count and the
org's month-to-date spend and credit balance, read live from IAM and commerce.

The rows are the caller's tenant window, not the fleet: a SuperAdmin gets every org, a
white-label admin only their own subtree. A per-org read that fails degrades THAT row
to an honest zero — this panel carries no sources[] channel to report freshness on, so
the alternative would be a fleet total that silently reads healthy.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Page is the 1-based page number. Defaults to "1".

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
PageSize is rows per page. Defaults to "200", the shared admin page size.
It bounds the fan-out: the page decides how many per-org reads happen, so
the directory costs the same at eighty tenants and at eight thousand.

get.summary: Is the Platform Overview tiles: how many orgs and users are in the caller's tenant window, the fleet workload counts, and month-to-date spend and credits.
get.description:
Is the Platform Overview tiles: how many orgs and users are in the caller's
tenant window, the fleet workload counts, and month-to-date spend and credits.

It ALWAYS answers 200 — a tile board that fails as a whole because one upstream is
down is useless. Instead every upstream reports itself in sources[]: ok, degraded, or
not-configured. A commerce read that failed for ANY org marks that source degraded,
because the spend/credits totals are then an undercount and must not read healthy.

The AI tiles — 30-day spend and tokens — come from the AI ledger (ledger.go), the
plane that owns "what was served". They used to come from the money plane with the
token counter hardcoded to zero, so the board read $0.00 and 0 tokens over a month in
which the fleet served fifteen thousand requests. Credits still come from commerce,
which owns the wallet.

get.summary: Lists the fleet workload registry: every operator App CR across the platform namespaces with its declared vs running image tag, reconciled health/phase and drift verdict.
get.description:
Lists the fleet workload registry: every operator App CR across the platform
namespaces with its declared vs running image tag, reconciled health/phase and drift
verdict. Optionally narrowed by kind, tier or env, each an exact match.

The rows are the SAME observation /v1/platform/fleet renders — read through the in-process
platform seam, not a second k8s client — so the two boards can never disagree about what
the fleet is. A PaaS plane that is not co-resident yields an honestly empty registry,
never a fabricated row.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind matches the operator App CR's declared spec.role (sql|kv|generic|ingress).

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: Tier matches the derived infra grouping (cloud|data|edge|daemon|paas|app).

parameters.name: env
parameters.description: Env matches the lifecycle namespace (main|test|dev).

get.summary: Reads the current platform plan promo — the singleton discount offer, e.g.
get.description:
Reads the current platform plan promo — the singleton discount offer, e.g.
the 50%-off launch promo. Commerce stores it in the reserved platform namespace, so
the org sent with the read is the admin org and the service token is what passes
commerce's own platform-admin gate.

put.summary: Upserts the platform plan promo — the ONE place the offer is configured.
put.description:
Upserts the platform plan promo — the ONE place the offer is configured.

The body is commerce's own promo contract and is forwarded BYTE-FOR-BYTE, so no field
commerce accepts is dropped in transit. promoIn names its documented fields.

get.summary: Serves GET /v1/admin/providers/credit — the per-provider upstream credit ledger.
get.description:
Serves GET /v1/admin/providers/credit — the per-provider upstream
credit ledger. SuperAdmin-guarded (see Routes).

get.summary: Is the fleet money board: total prepaid balances held, total realized spend, MRR, ARPU, a per-customer table sorted highest-revenue first, and a real 30-day spend trend from the usage ledger.
get.description:
Is the fleet money board: total prepaid balances held, total realized spend,
MRR, ARPU, a per-customer table sorted highest-revenue first, and a real 30-day spend
trend from the usage ledger.

ORTHOGONAL to /v1/admin/finance, which is the COGS/margin view of what WE pay vendors.
This is the customer side: what each customer holds, spends and subscribes to.

arpu divides realized spend by PAYING customers, not by all of them — a fleet of free
signups must not deflate the number. A customer counts as paying when it has spend or
MRR.

An org whose money did not read degrades to honest zeros and marks the commerce source
degraded in sources[], so a partial fleet read is visible instead of quietly low.

get.summary: Lists IAM roles for one owner org, forwarded VERBATIM from IAM's get-roles.
get.description: Lists IAM roles for one owner org, forwarded VERBATIM from IAM's get-roles.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description:
Owner is the org whose rows to read. Defaults to the admin org, which owns the
platform's roles and applications.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description:
Page is the 1-based page number. Forwarded only when set — IAM applies its own
default otherwise.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: PageSize is rows per page. Forwarded only when set.

get.summary: Reads the launch board: every hosted service in the registry with its LIVE waitlist mode, evaluated through the flag engine.
get.description:
Reads the launch board: every hosted service in the registry with its LIVE
waitlist mode, evaluated through the flag engine. This is the "remove the waitlist one
service at a time" view.

post.summary: Onboards a hosted service, or edits one, so a new host comes under the launch gate WITHOUT a redeploy.
post.description:
Onboards a hosted service, or edits one, so a new host comes under the
launch gate WITHOUT a redeploy. Re-registering an existing service PRESERVES its live
switch — editing the hosts of a service that is already open must not silently close
it again.

post.summary: Flips ONE service's waitlist switch — the launch lever.
post.description:
Flips ONE service's waitlist switch — the launch lever. Hot: it takes
effect on this pod immediately and on peers within one evaluation TTL, with no
redeploy. An unknown service is a 404, not a silent create; onboarding goes through
upsertService.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Service is the slug to flip, taken from the path.

get.summary: Answers GET /v1/admin/subscriptions.
get.description:
Answers GET /v1/admin/subscriptions.

	GET /v1/admin/subscriptions?org=&status=&limit=

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status filters on the subscription's LATEST lifecycle status (active, trialing,
canceled, …), matched case-insensitively.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org filters to one tenant, matched exactly.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned. total still reports the full match count.

get.summary: subsystems answers GET /v1/admin/subsystems.
get.description:
subsystems answers GET /v1/admin/subsystems. ?range=24h|7d|30d bounds the telemetry
window (default 30d) — the same enum, and the same helpers, as the o11y board.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range bounds the telemetry window: 24h, 7d or 30d. Anything else, including
empty, resolves to the default through the same o11yRange the o11y board uses.

post.description:
Answers the operator's "Sync now" button. There is nothing to kick: admin
aggregates LIVE on every read, so the button is just a re-read. It acknowledges
honestly with started:true rather than pretending a batch job was queued.

get.summary: Returns the trailing 30 days of AI usage: one org's when org names one, else the whole fleet's — the spend, the tokens and the requests, the daily curve behind them, and the split by model.
get.description:
Returns the trailing 30 days of AI usage: one org's when org names one, else the
whole fleet's — the spend, the tokens and the requests, the daily curve behind them,
and the split by model.

It reads the AI ledger (ledger.go), which is the plane that owns this question. It used
to ask the commerce billing API instead, once per org, and answer with a hardcoded
empty series, zero tokens and zero requests, on the reasoning that a trend and a split
were "not derivable from the commerce billing API". They are not — but the question was
never commerce's. hanzo.cloud_usage carries a row per served request, so all three fall
out of the same window the totals do.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org reads ONE tenant's trailing-30-day total instead of the fleet sum. Honoured
for a SuperAdmin only — a white-label admin always reads their own org.

The window is the one core.OrgMoney returns, and it is what the operator board
beside this already labelled ("Daily, last 30 days"). The wire used to say
month-to-date while that UI said 30 days; they agree now. This comment is
REGENERATED into plugin/admin/openapi.json and openapi.yaml as the ?org
parameter description, so a stale word here ships as a contradiction inside
one spec file — which is the drift this whole change set exists to remove.

get.summary: Splits our upstream AI usage by how it was FUNDED: one row per (provider, model) over the window, tagged credit (provider grant still remaining), paid (grant exhausted) or paid_only (no grant at all).
get.description:
Splits our upstream AI usage by how it was FUNDED: one row per (provider,
model) over the window, tagged credit (provider grant still remaining), paid (grant
exhausted) or paid_only (no grant at all).

The class is resolved at the PROVIDER level from the credit ledger, not per call — the
per-call split, and the `byo` class, arrive when the metering write stamps a funding
column on cloud_usage and this can GROUP BY it directly. Until then a provider with
remaining grant reports all of its usage as credit, which is right in aggregate and
approximate at the boundary where a grant runs out mid-window.

An unparseable window falls back to the last 30 days rather than refusing: this is a
dashboard read, and a typo in a date must not blank the board.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
From is the inclusive start of the window. Unparseable or absent, together with
To, falls back to the last 30 days.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: To is the exclusive end of the window.

get.summary: Lists the user directory across the caller's tenant window, one page at a time.
get.description:
Lists the user directory across the caller's tenant window, one page at a time.
total is IAM's REAL total, so the console can page through it.

A SuperAdmin may aim the read at one tenant with org; a white-label admin cannot — for
them the owner is hard-pinned to their own org and org is ignored, which is what keeps
the directory from becoming a cross-tenant read.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description:
Org narrows the directory to ONE tenant. Honoured for a SuperAdmin only — a
white-label admin is pinned to their own org and this is ignored.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Query is a free-text filter, matched by IAM as a "contains" over the user name.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description:
Page is the 1-based page number. Defaults to "1"; IAM returns zero rows AND a
zero total when it is unset, so this layer never leaves it empty.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: PageSize is rows per page. Defaults to "200", the shared admin page size.

get.summary: Returns the realtime block-storage board: the DigitalOcean volume fleet (count, capacity, monthly list cost, per-volume region and attachment) plus the analytics datastore's OWN fill, read from its system.disks.
get.description:
Returns the realtime block-storage board: the DigitalOcean volume fleet
(count, capacity, monthly list cost, per-volume region and attachment) plus the
analytics datastore's OWN fill, read from its system.disks.

A volume's usedGiB and pct are null, always: DO exposes capacity and attachment but no
fill, so the console renders "—" rather than a number nobody measured. The datastore
card is the one real fill here, and it is the number to scale on.

The two sources degrade independently — a DO outage still returns the datastore fill,
and a disconnected datastore still returns the DO fleet. What a DO outage must NOT do
is pass for an account with no volumes, so the fleet it could not read is marked
incomplete rather than reported as a count of zero at a cost of zero.

get.summary: Reads one waitlist's leaderboard from the Hanzo waitlist engine — position, points and referral standing per entry — proxied server-authed with the engine secret, never a client credential.
get.description:
Reads one waitlist's leaderboard from the Hanzo waitlist engine — position,
points and referral standing per entry — proxied server-authed with the engine secret,
never a client credential.

The engine's payload is forwarded VERBATIM as data; the console normalizes it. When
the engine is not configured on this deployment the read still succeeds, with an empty
object and a msg saying so, so the panel shows an honest not-wired state instead of an
error the operator would chase.

parameters.name: waitlist
parameters.description:
Waitlist is the waitlist slug to read (e.g. "chat"). The engine decides what an
empty slug means.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page is the 1-based page number.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: PageSize is entries per page.

post.summary: Grants a user waitlist points, moving them up toward the access cutoff.
post.description:
Grants a user waitlist points, moving them up toward the access cutoff.
This is the access lever: the cutoff itself does not move, the person does.

It funnels through the engine's verified grant seam (POST /v1/waitlist/award with
source="grant" — the ONE path that honours an explicit points amount) and writes a
tamper-evident audit row either way, so a FAILED grant is recorded too. The reason
field goes only to that row.

affected.description: Affected lists the usernames that were updated.

failed.description:
Failed lists the usernames that were NOT updated. Non-empty means the org is in
a mixed state and the action should be retried.

org.description: Org is the tenant acted on.

suspended.description: Suspended is the state applied: true for suspend, false for reactivate.

data.description:
Data is the per-user breakdown of what changed. Null exactly when Status is
"error", which means no user was touched.

msg.description:
Msg is why the action could not run at all: no org named, the org unknown (also
HTTP 404), or IAM's member list unreadable. Empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", and it answers whether the action RAN, not whether every
user was updated. A partial failure is an ok answer with a non-empty data.failed —
read that before treating the org as fully suspended.

org.description:
Org is the tenant to migrate. Required — there is no fleet-wide form of this
cutover, because each org must be reconciled on its own.

data.description:
Data is the receipt. Null exactly when Status is "error". A retry is safe: the
deposit carries the fixed ref "backfill:<org>", so the wallet is credited at most
once however many times this runs.

msg.description:
Msg is why, and is empty on success. It names the half that failed: "read commerce
balance: ..." before any money moved, "finance backfill: ..." at the write.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". Error means NOTHING was carried — the commerce balance
is read and must be readable before the wallet is written, so an unreadable source
refuses the cutover rather than migrating a phantom zero.

entryId.description:
EntryID is the finance ledger entry created, or "" when the balance was
non-positive and there was nothing to carry.

migratedCents.description: MigratedCents is the balance carried across, read from commerce BEFORE the move.

org.description: Org is the tenant migrated.

auditUrl.description: AuditURL is where the change log for those writes lives: /v1/flags/activity.

configured.description:
Configured is whether the definition stores opened. When false every switch
below is resolving from env or its registered default — the values are still
the ones in force, but nothing stored can be reaching them and a write will
fail. That is the fail-safe posture, not an outage.

engine.description:
Engine names the evaluator serving these values: "hanzo-flags", running
in-process in this pod.

manageUrl.description:
ManageURL is where the definitions behind these switches are read and
written: /v1/flags/defs.

switches.description:
Switches is every registered switch with the value in force, in registration
order — the seeded platform set first, then whatever each subsystem added at
init. The registry is open, so this is the deployment's switchboard rather
than a fixed list.

id.description:
ID is the DOKS cluster UUID — the same UUID that appears in a resource's
`k8s:<uuid>` tag, and the key every scan and every proven ownership joins on.

idlePVCs.description:
IdlePVCs is how many of this cluster's volumes are Bound with no pod mounting them
— its share of the review queue, not of the delete queue.

monthlyCents.description:
MonthlyCents is this cluster's share of the bill: its droplets plus the volumes
PROVEN to belong to it. Load balancers are not included — a Service's load balancer
is attributed on the load-balancer row, not folded in here, so cluster costs never
double-count against Cost.totalMonthly.

name.description:
Name is the cluster's DO name ("hanzo-k8s"). It is what every human-facing message
on this board names a cluster by, including the refusal reasons.

nodePools.description: NodePools is how many pools the cluster has, which is len(pools).

nodes.description:
Nodes is how many droplets carry this cluster's tag. It comes from the DO
inventory, so it is populated even for a cluster that never answered.

pods.description:
Pods is how many pods the scan listed, all namespaces. Zero when Scanned is false —
unknown, not empty.

pools.description: Pools is the pools themselves, each carrying its own scale verdict.

pvcs.description: PVCs is how many PersistentVolumeClaims the scan listed.

pvs.description:
PVs is how many PersistentVolumes the scan listed. These are the claims that make a
DO volume live; zero here with Scanned false is what forces the whole board
incomplete.

region.description:
Region is DO's region slug ("nyc3"). A volume can only ever attach to a droplet in
its own region, which is why the region rides along on the row.

scanError.description:
ScanError is why the scan failed, or "not scanned" when the cluster was never
reached at all. Empty exactly when Scanned is true.

scanned.description:
Scanned reports that this cluster's Kubernetes answered. False makes the whole
board incomplete, not just this row: a cluster that did not answer might hold any
volume on it.

status.description:
Status is DOKS's own lifecycle state for the control plane ("running",
"provisioning", "degraded", "error", "deleting"). It says nothing about whether
this board reached the cluster — Scanned answers that.

version.description: Version is the DOKS Kubernetes version DO reports ("1.31.1-do.0").

cordon.description: Cordon true marks the node unschedulable; false restores it.

drain.description: Drain additionally evicts the pods already running there.

id.description: ID is the node's droplet id, from the path.

dropletsMonthly.description:
DropletsMonthly is DigitalOcean's list price for every droplet's size, summed.
The droplet's local disk is part of that price and is never billed again.

loadBalancersMonthly.description:
LoadBalancersMonthly is $12 per billed node per month, summed. DO's API does not
price load balancers, so this is derived from the size_unit it does report.

reclaimableMonthly.description:
ReclaimableMonthly is what deleting the unreferenced volumes would stop costing —
the one figure on this board that a button here can actually collect. Zero while
Complete is false, because an unproven orphan is not an orphan.

totalMonthly.description:
TotalMonthly is droplets + volumes + load balancers. It is the fleet's recurring
bill, not the DigitalOcean invoice: bandwidth, snapshots, spaces and registry are
not inventory this board reads. WastedMonthly is already inside VolumesMonthly and
is never added again.

volumesMonthly.description:
VolumesMonthly is block storage at DO's rate of 10 cents per provisioned GiB per
month, summed over every volume — attached, idle and orphaned alike, because DO
bills for capacity, not for use.

wastedMonthly.description:
WastedMonthly is what the fleet pays every month for provisioned-but-empty space on
the volumes a kubelet actually measured.

It is NOT ReclaimableMonthly and must never be added to it. Reclaimable is money a
button on this board collects, by deleting volumes proven to belong to no one.
Wasted is money locked inside volumes that are IN USE and holding live data:
DigitalOcean can only ever grow a volume, so collecting it means copying a database
onto a smaller one. See shrinkRecipe.

It is also a LOWER BOUND — unmeasured volumes contribute nothing.

apiKeys.description:
APIKeys is how many members hold an access key — the org's programmatic reach,
counted from users[] and never the keys themselves.

balanceCents.description: BalanceCents is the prepaid wallet still held, in USD cents.

created.description: Created is when IAM created the org, RFC3339.

display.description: Display is the org's display name, falling back to the slug when it has none.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents, over the subscriptions
commerce counts as revenue. A trial contributes zero while still naming Plan.

org.description: Org is the tenant slug, echoed from the path.

ownerEmail.description:
OwnerEmail is the org admin's email, or the first member with one. Empty when no
member carries an email.

plan.description: Plan is the live subscription tier's name, or "pay-as-you-go" with no subscription.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is metered consumption over the trailing 30 days, in USD cents.

status.description:
Status is `active` or `suspended` — suspended only when the org has members and
every one of them is forbidden. The per-member truth is in users[].forbidden.

transactions.description:
Transactions is the org's ledger, newest first, capped at the last 50 entries. A
sample of the history, not the whole of it, so the balance above cannot be
recomputed by folding this.

users.description:
Users is the org's members, up to a 200-member page. Suspend and reactivate act on
exactly this set.

data.description: Data is the customer. Null exactly when Status is "error".

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". An unknown org is an error and also carries HTTP 404 —
the status code is the addition, not a different contract.

balanceCents.description:
BalanceCents is the prepaid wallet the org still holds, in USD cents. What is left
to spend, not what was granted.

created.description: Created is when IAM created the org, RFC3339 — the signup date.

display.description:
Display is the org's display name, falling back to the slug when it has none. For
humans; never key on it.

lastActive.description:
LastActive is the most recent sign-in across every member, RFC3339. The best
activity signal IAM carries, so it tracks people logging in, not API traffic. Empty
when no member has ever signed in.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is the org's monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents: commerce's own
per-subscription figure, already interval-normalized and multiplied by seats, summed
over the subscriptions commerce counts as revenue. A trial contributes zero.

org.description:
Org is the tenant slug — the row's identity, and the value every per-customer route
takes in its path. The list is sorted by it.

ownerEmail.description:
OwnerEmail is the org admin's email, or the first member with one. Empty when no
member carries an email at all — IAM does not require one.

plan.description:
Plan is the name of the org's live subscription tier, or "pay-as-you-go" for a
metered customer with no subscription. A trial names its plan here even though it
contributes no MRR.

spendCents.description:
SpendCents is metered consumption over the TRAILING 30 DAYS, in USD cents — the one
window every fleet money surface means by "spend". Positive, and it does not reset
on the first of the month.

status.description:
Status is `active` or `suspended`, derived from the members' IAM isForbidden flags.
Suspended requires the org to have members and EVERY one of them to be forbidden —
a partly-forbidden org still reads active, because some of it can still sign in.

users.description:
Users is how many members IAM lists for the org, up to the 200-member page this
read takes. Every other IAM-derived field on the row is folded from that same page.

cents.description:
Cents is the entry's magnitude in minor units, and it is UNSIGNED — a withdraw
does not arrive negative, so a running balance has to be folded by reading Type.

currency.description: Currency is the entry's ISO code, lower-cased. "usd" throughout the fleet today.

id.description: ID is the commerce ledger entry id — what reconciliation against commerce joins on.

notes.description:
Notes is the free-text memo the entry was written with — for a staff grant, the
reason an operator typed. Omitted when blank.

time.description: Time is when the entry was recorded, RFC3339. The history is newest first.

type.description:
Type is `deposit` (money in: a top-up or a staff grant) or `withdraw` (money out:
metered usage). It is the only thing that gives Cents its direction.

created.description: Created is when IAM created the member, RFC3339.

email.description: Email is the member's address, empty when IAM holds none.

forbidden.description:
Forbidden is IAM's isForbidden. True means IAM refuses this user at login AND at
token issuance, so they can neither sign in nor mint a fresh one. It is what
suspend sets and reactivate clears, per user — which is why an org can sit in a
mixed state after a partial failure.

hasApiKey.description:
HasAPIKey reports that the member holds an access key. PRESENCE only: the key
itself is never read onto this surface.

isAdmin.description:
IsAdmin is admin OF THIS ORG — the customer's own account owner, who manages their
members and apps. It is NOT platform privilege: SuperAdmin is membership of the
reserved `admin` org and never appears on a customer row.

lastSignin.description:
LastSignin is the member's most recent sign-in, RFC3339. Empty means never signed
in — which is different from signed in long ago.

name.description:
Name is the IAM username, unique within the org. `<org>/<name>` is the id the
suspend and reactivate actions address the user by.

data.description: Data is every customer org, sorted by slug.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". An error here means the IAM org directory could not be
read; a per-org money or plan failure does not fail the fleet, it degrades that
row's field to its zero.

total.description:
Total is len(data). The list is unpaginated, so it is a convenience, never a
count of rows withheld. Omitted on an error.

accountBalanceCents.description:
AccountBalanceCents is DigitalOcean's raw account balance, sign INCLUDED: positive
means we owe DO, negative means we hold credit. It is here so the sign convention
is visible rather than only implied by CreditRemainingCents.

avgDailyBurnCents.description:
AvgDailyBurnCents is month-to-date spend divided by the elapsed days of the current
month, at least one. A running average, so it is noisiest on the 1st and steadies
through the month. It is the denominator of runwayDays.

configured.description:
Configured reports that a DO_API_TOKEN is set and the balance read succeeded. False
zeroes every number below and makes runwayDays null rather than infinite.

creditRemainingCents.description:
CreditRemainingCents is the promo credit still held, in USD cents, POSITIVE. It is
the negated account balance, clamped at zero: DigitalOcean carries an
accounts-receivable sign, so credit we hold shows as a NEGATIVE balance and an
amount we owe shows positive — an account we owe on has zero credit, not negative.

error.description:
Error is why the DO read failed, or that the token is unset. Omitted when
Configured is true.

generatedAt.description:
GeneratedAt is when DigitalOcean generated the balance, from their response — not
when this board read it. Omitted when DO did not say.

history.description:
History is the burn-down series, up to the last 60 billing entries. Best effort: a
failed history read leaves it empty while the balance above still stands, so an
empty series is not evidence of no spend. Never null.

monthToDateSpendCents.description:
MonthToDateSpendCents is what DigitalOcean has charged this calendar month, in USD
cents. It resets on the first, which is why the burn below divides by the day of
the month and not by a fixed 30.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the entry in USD cents, converted once from DO's decimal-dollar
string. It carries DO's own accounts-receivable sign: a usage charge is positive.

date.description: Date is when DigitalOcean recorded the entry, RFC3339 as they return it.

description.description: Description is DigitalOcean's own line text for the entry.

type.description:
Type is DigitalOcean's entry type — "Invoice", "Payment", "Credit". Entries are not
all charges, so summing the series without reading this mixes money in with money
out.

disk.description:
Disk requests a PERMANENT resize that grows the disk. DO can never resize such a
droplet down again, so it defaults false — a CPU/RAM-only change, reversible.

id.description: ID is the DO droplet id, from the path. Numeric.

size.description: Size is the target DigitalOcean size slug on resize, e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb".

configured.description:
Configured reports that commerce answered the COGS read. False makes every number
below a zero that was never measured — the margin is still computed from it, so a
board showing a healthy margin with configured=false is showing revenue minus
nothing.

digitalocean.description:
DigitalOcean is the promo-credit treasury view. It is deliberately NOT part of
COGS and is never added to TotalCents — the DO spend it reports is already inside
the vendor lines above. It feeds runway, and only runway.

error.description:
Error is why the COGS read failed, or that commerce is not wired at all. Omitted
when Configured is true.

period.description:
Period is the billing month the COGS covers, "2006-01". Commerce's own period where
it gave one, otherwise the current month.

totalCents.description:
TotalCents is whole-platform COGS for the period, in USD cents — commerce's figure,
not a sum of Vendors recomputed here. It is the number the margin subtracts.

vendors.description:
Vendors is the per-vendor breakdown behind that total. Never null; empty when
commerce is unreachable.

cost.description:
Cost is COGS: what the fleet pays its vendors, plus the DigitalOcean credit
treasury view that only runway is derived from.

derived.description:
Derived is the profitability math over the two above. A pure function of them, so
it can be recomputed by hand and checked.

generatedAt.description: GeneratedAt is when the read ran, RFC3339. Nothing on this board is cached.

revenue.description: Revenue is what the fleet earned — consumption and MRR, from commerce.

sources.description:
Sources is the freshness strip: "commerce-costs", "digitalocean" and "commerce".
A not-ok row is the ONLY thing separating a real zero from an upstream that was
never read — the margin below is computed either way.

grossMarginCents.description:
GrossMarginCents is revenue.totalRevenueCents minus cost.totalCents, in USD cents.
Negative means the fleet spent more on vendors than its customers consumed.

grossMarginPct.description:
GrossMarginPct is that margin as a percentage of revenue — 42.5 means 42.5%, not
0.425. Zero when revenue is zero, which is arithmetic, not a claim of break-even.

profitable.description:
Profitable is revenue strictly greater than COGS — the sign of GrossMarginCents,
stated so no consumer has to decide what zero means. It is GROSS margin only:
salaries, tooling and anything outside vendor COGS are not in this.

runwayDays.description:
RunwayDays is DigitalOcean promo credit divided by average daily burn — how long
the credit lasts at today's rate, and nothing to do with the margin above. NULL,
never a large number, when DO is unconfigured or burn is zero: no honest projection
exists, and an infinity would read as safety.

data.description: Data is the board. Never null on an ok answer.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". Every upstream on this board degrades in place — an
unreachable commerce or an unset DO token answers ok with configured=false and a
not-ok source — so an error here means admission itself failed, not the numbers.

configured.description:
Configured reports that the org directory was read and at least the ledger
answered. False means the numbers below are zeros nobody measured — and since the
margin is revenue minus COGS, that zero reads as a loss rather than as unknown.

creditsConsumedCents.description:
CreditsConsumedCents is the same figure as TotalRevenueCents, named for the other
side of the identity: what the fleet earned is exactly what its customers burned.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is fleet monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents, summed over every org's
revenue-counting subscriptions. Contract value, and a different question from
TotalRevenueCents — it is not folded into the margin.

totalRevenueCents.description:
TotalRevenueCents is fleet consumption over the trailing 30 days, in USD cents,
summed across every org. Realized revenue: credit is revenue when it is SPENT, not
when it is granted.

cluster.description: Cluster is the cluster's name where the finding is scoped to one, "" otherwise.

detail.description:
Detail is the full explanation. For an oversized volume it is the entire
copy-and-swap migration, written out as kubectl steps — this board prints the
recipe and deliberately refuses to run it.

id.description:
ID is stable across scans and unique within one: `unref/<volume>`,
`oversized/<volume>`, `pod/<cluster>/<ns>/<name>`, `image/<repo>`,
`cost/node/<name>`. A consumer can key a dismissal off it.

kind.description:
Kind is the machine-readable class: `scan-incomplete`, `unreferenced-volume`,
`released-pv`, `idle-pvc`, `oversized-volume`, `pod-unhealthy`, `unknown-image`,
`cost-outlier`. Group and filter on this; Title is for a human.

monthlyCents.description:
MonthlyCents is the money at stake, and it is the secondary sort within a severity.
It carries what acting would actually SAVE, not the raw waste — an oversized volume
reports the saving after keeping headroom, since a list sorted by money has to be
sorted by money you could really get back. Zero when nothing is at stake.

resource.description:
Resource is what the finding is about, in that kind's own addressing: a volume id,
a `namespace/name` pod, an image repository. Empty on a fleet-wide finding.

severity.description:
Severity is one of `critical`, `warn`, `info`, and is the primary sort. Only an
incomplete scan is critical, because only that invalidates the board's other
answers.

title.description: Title is the one-line summary, already carrying the numbers that matter.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the credit, in whole cents. Must be positive and within the
per-grant cap.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO code, lower-cased. Empty means usd.

org.description: Org is the tenant to credit. Required.

reason.description: Reason is the operator's justification, recorded on the audit row.

source.description:
Source is the money bucket: "trial" (default) for a non-cash comp that is never
refundable, or "prepaid" for real money. Anything unknown falls back to trial.

user.description:
User optionally names a MEMBER to credit, by bare IAM username. Empty credits
the org. Which of the two the money actually lands on is decided by
account.Payer, not here: a pooled org keeps one balance whatever is named.

data.description:
Data is the receipt: the account credited, the amount, and the balance after.
Null exactly when Status is "error".

msg.description:
Msg is why the grant was refused, and is empty on success. Two refusals also carry
a non-200 HTTP status alongside this envelope: 404 for an unknown org, 503 when
there is nowhere durable to record the grant.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". Error means NO money moved: every refusal — a
non-positive amount, one over the per-grant cap, an unknown org, a deployment with
no durable audit store — is decided before the ledger is written.

balanceCents.description: BalanceCents is the account balance AFTER the grant, in whole cents.

balanceExact.description:
BalanceExact is that same balance at full 18-decimal precision, so a sub-cent
debit is visible rather than rounded away.

currency.description: Currency is the lower-cased ISO code the grant was denominated in.

grantedCents.description: GrantedCents is the amount actually credited.

org.description: Org is the tenant whose ledger was credited.

source.description: Source is the money bucket: "trial" (non-cash comp) or "prepaid" (real money).

subject.description:
Subject is the ACCOUNT the credit landed on inside that ledger: the org slug for
a pooled org, "<org>/<name>" for a member of a per-member one. It is echoed
because the operator does not choose it — account.Payer does — so naming a
member of a pooled org credits the pool and the receipt has to say so.

transactionId.description: TransactionID is the ledger entry id, for reconciliation against commerce.

actor.description: staff email (or sub) who issued it

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the credit in USD cents, always positive. On a successful grant it
is what was actually written to the ledger; on a REFUSED one it is what was asked
for and never moved, so summing this column without filtering on Result overstates
what the fleet gave away.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the grant was attempted, RFC3339 in UTC. The list is newest first.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO code the grant was denominated in, lower-cased. Defaults to
"usd" for a row that recorded none.

org.description:
Org is the TARGET tenant the credit landed on — the audit row's resource id, not
the actor's org. The `org` query filter matches the actor's, which is the one
asymmetry on this surface.

reason.description:
Reason is the justification the operator typed. Omitted when blank — older rows
predate the field.

transactionId.description:
TransactionID is the commerce ledger entry the money landed in, for reconciliation.
Omitted on a refused grant, which wrote no entry.

data.description:
Data is the matching grants, newest first, capped by the request's limit. Refused
grants are included — a refusal is as much a fact about who tried as a success is.

msg.description:
Msg carries that "no audit store" note ALONGSIDE an ok status. Everywhere else on
this app a non-empty msg means failure; here it means the history is unavailable,
which is why an empty list must not be read as "no grants were ever made".

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A deployment with no durable audit store has no history
to project and still answers ok — with an empty list and a msg saying so.

total.description:
Total is the store's count for the filter, which EXCEEDS len(data) when limit
truncated. Omitted on an error.

brokenAt.description:
BrokenAt is the seq of the FIRST record that failed verification, and -1
whenever the walk found no break (including an unread chain, where no seq
was reached).

count.description:
Count is the number of records walked. Zero on an unread chain, where it
means "nothing was read", not "the chain is empty".

head.description:
Head is the hash of the last record (or the genesis anchor for an empty
chain). Pin this externally over time to detect tail-truncation.

name.description:
Name is the chain this verdict is about, e.g. "audit" or "audit-iam". It is
carried because a verdict with no chain on it reads as the whole trail's,
which is what a reader of a 128-chain deployment did.

reason.description:
Reason says HOW the chain fails at BrokenAt — a recomputed-hash mismatch, a
prev-hash discontinuity, or a seq gap — or, on an unread chain, why it could
not be walked at all. Absent on an intact chain, which is the only verdict
with nothing to explain.

verdict.description: Verdict is intact, broken or unread.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the invoice total in minor units of Currency, as of its latest
event. It is the amount BILLED — a partially paid invoice does not report a
remainder here.

currency.description:
Currency is the invoice's ISO code. AmountCents is minor units of THIS, so a list
spanning currencies must not be summed without reading it.

display.description:
Display is the same slug as Org. The warehouse holds no friendly name and this
read does no per-org IAM fan-out, so it repeats the slug rather than inventing one.

due.description: Due is when payment is due, RFC3339. Empty when the invoice carries no due date.

id.description:
ID is commerce's invoice id — the row's identity, and what a detail view fetches
/v1/billing/invoices/:id with.

issued.description:
Issued is when the invoice was issued, RFC3339 as commerce emitted it. The list is
sorted by it, newest first.

number.description:
Number is the human invoice number the customer sees on the document. Distinct from
ID, which is the machine handle.

org.description: Org is the tenant the invoice was issued to, and what ?org= matches exactly.

status.description:
Status is the EFFECTIVE lifecycle state, folded from the invoice's latest event:
`paid` and `void` are terminal and come from the event itself; anything else is the
last status the events carried, defaulting to `open` for a finalized invoice.

data.description: Data is the matching invoices, newest issued first, capped by limit.

msg.description: Msg is the query failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A warehouse that is not connected answers ok with an
empty list and total 0 — the honest not-yet-wired state, not a claim that the fleet
has never invoiced anyone.

total.description:
Total is how many matched BEFORE limit truncated, so a console can say "showing 50
of 812". Omitted on an error.

blockedReason.description:
BlockedReason is why not — which Service still wants it, or how many of its member
droplets sit outside every cluster and so cannot be vouched for. Empty exactly when
Deletable is true.

cluster.description:
Cluster is the owning cluster's name — from the claiming Service where there is
one, otherwise from the cluster its member droplets belong to.

deletable.description:
Deletable is the standing verdict: no live Service claims it, every member droplet
belongs to a cluster this board scanned, and the scan was complete.

droplets.description:
Droplets is how many droplets it forwards to. NOT a liveness signal: a DOKS load
balancer lists every node in its cluster, so a leaked one still looks busy.

id.description:
ID is the DO load balancer UUID. DOKS writes it into the Service's
`kubernetes.digitalocean.com/load-balancer-id` annotation, which is one of the two
identities the liveness index is keyed by.

ip.description:
IP is the public address it answers on — the address that black-holes if it is
deleted while a Service still wants it. It is also the second identity the
liveness index matches on, for a Service that carries no annotation.

monthlyCents.description:
MonthlyCents is SizeUnit at $12 per node per month. Derived, because DO's API
prices droplets but not load balancers.

name.description:
Name is DigitalOcean's own name for it. A DOKS-provisioned load balancer is named
after neither its Service nor its cluster, so this does not identify who uses it —
Service does.

service.description:
Service is the `namespace/name` of the live type=LoadBalancer Service that claims
this load balancer, proven from the cluster scan. Non-empty means IN USE.

sizeUnit.description:
SizeUnit is the number of billed load-balancer nodes DO reports. Never below 1: DO
omits the field on the legacy single-node size, which is one node, not zero.

status.description: Status is DO's own state for it ("new", "active", "errored").

blockedReason.description:
BlockedReason is why not, in the operator's language, and it names the lever that
DOES work — scale or edit the node pool. Empty exactly when Mutable is true.

cluster.description:
Cluster is the DOKS cluster's name, or "" for a droplet no cluster owns — the only
kind this board will ever delete.

clusterId.description:
ClusterID is that cluster's UUID, read from the droplet's own `k8s:<uuid>` tag. On
a DROPLET the tag is authoritative, unlike on a volume: DOKS creates the droplet
and destroys it with the pool, so the tag cannot outlive what it describes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when DO created the droplet, RFC3339.

id.description: ID is the DigitalOcean droplet id. Numeric, and the id every droplet route takes.

localDiskGiB.description:
LocalDiskGiB is the droplet's own disk, in GiB. Its price is already inside
MonthlyCents — DO does not bill it as block storage, and adding it to the volume
totals is how a fleet appears to hold terabytes it never pays for.

memoryMiB.description: MemoryMiB is the plan's RAM, in MiB as DO reports it.

monthlyCents.description:
MonthlyCents is DO's list price for SizeSlug, in cents per month. It is the plan's
price, not a metered bill, so it does not move with how hard the machine works.

mutable.description:
Mutable reports whether this droplet may be changed DIRECTLY — deleted or resized.
One predicate covers both because one fact decides both: a DOKS node belongs to a
node pool, and the pool is the only thing allowed to change it.

name.description:
Name is the droplet name. For a DOKS node it is also the Kubernetes node name, and
that equality is the join: it is how Ready, Schedulable and Pods below get filled.

pods.description: Pods is how many pods the scan found scheduled on this node.

privateIp.description: PrivateIP is the droplet's VPC address, or "" when it has none.

publicIp.description: PublicIP is the droplet's internet-facing address, or "" when it has none.

ready.description:
Ready is the Kubernetes node's own Ready condition, joined by Name. False for a
droplet that is not a node at all, and for a node in a cluster that did not answer
— unknown reads as not-ready, which refuses more and is the safe direction.

schedulable.description:
Schedulable is the same node's cordon state, inverted: false means unschedulable.
It is what the cordon route sets, and only a Ready AND schedulable node counts
toward NodePool.clusterSchedulable.

sizeSlug.description:
SizeSlug is the DigitalOcean plan ("s-4vcpu-8gb"). It decides MonthlyCents and is
what a resize sets.

status.description:
Status is DO's droplet state ("new", "active", "off", "archive"). A powered-off
droplet still bills, which is why "off" here and a cost row are not in tension.

tags.description:
Tags are DO's resource tags verbatim, including the DOKS stamps `k8s:<uuid>` and
`k8s:worker`. Never null — an untagged droplet carries an empty list.

vcpus.description: VCPUs is the plan's virtual CPU count.

volumes.description: Volumes is how many block-storage volumes DO reports attached to this droplet.

generatedAt.description:
GeneratedAt is when the admin plane served this read, RFC3339. Same instant as
asOf: this board computes on demand and caches nothing, so the two cannot diverge.

sources.description:
Sources is the upstream freshness strip. Exactly one row, "billing-warehouse", and
its ok=false is what distinguishes a fleet with no revenue from a deployment where
the warehouse is not connected — both otherwise answer zeros.

data.description: Data is the board. Never null on an ok answer.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A warehouse that is not connected still answers ok, with
real zeros and a not-ok source row — an honest empty board rather than a failure.

data.description: Data is the consolidated board. Omitted when the caller was refused.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. A degraded upstream still
answers "ok" — it is reported in data.sources, because a consolidated board
that fails whole because one source is down is useless.

data.description:
Data is the per-action result, and is deliberately opaque: its keys differ by
action, and each handler's own description names them. Null on a refusal or a
failure — and on a partial failure it may carry what DID happen, such as the
snapshotId of an undo taken before a delete that then failed.

msg.description:
Msg is why, and is empty on success. "refusing: <reason>" is the board's verdict;
anything else is the change having been attempted and failed.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A REFUSAL is an error too, and reads differently from a
failure: msg opens "refusing: " and means the board proved the change unsafe and
never attempted it, so nothing changed.

blockedReason.description:
BlockedReason is why not, in the operator's language. Empty exactly when Scalable
is true — allowed carries no reason, blocked always names one.

cluster.description:
Cluster is that cluster's name, carried on the row so a refusal can say which
cluster a shrink would strand.

clusterId.description: ClusterID is the DOKS cluster this pool belongs to.

clusterSchedulable.description:
ClusterSchedulable is how many nodes in the WHOLE cluster are both Ready and
schedulable — not just this pool's. Cordoned and NotReady nodes are excluded,
because a shrink's evicted pods cannot land on them. It rides on the row so
ScaleTo is a pure method of the row and needs no second lookup.

count.description:
Count is how many nodes the pool is currently set to. It is the DECLARED count, so
it can lead reality while DOKS creates or drains machines.

id.description:
ID is the DO node pool UUID. The scale route accepts it or Name interchangeably,
since both are unique within a cluster.

name.description:
Name is the pool's name ("workers") — what an operator reads off the board and
what every message about a scale names.

scalable.description:
Scalable is the standing verdict: whether a scale may be attempted at all. It
reflects the shared completeness gate ONLY. Whether a PARTICULAR count is allowed
depends on the number asked for, which ScaleTo decides at request time.

size.description:
Size is the DigitalOcean size slug every node in this pool is created at
("s-4vcpu-8gb"). One slug per pool: it is the pool, not the droplet, that declares
what its machines are, which is why a hand-resized node gets reverted.

burn_cents.description:
BurnCents is what we have consumed against that grant, in USD cents. For
DigitalOcean it is grant minus remaining, floored at zero — derived from their
authoritative balance. For every other provider it is the all-time sum of
cost_cents in the usage warehouse, which is not windowed.

error.description:
Error names the read that did not answer — a revoked token passes the
is-it-configured check and fails here. Omitted on a healthy row. When it is set,
treat the classification as absent rather than as "no credit".

grant_cents.description:
GrantCents is the promo credit that provider has issued us, in USD cents. For
DigitalOcean it is DISCOVERED from their own invoices, never declared: the
hand-entered number was wrong by ~$22k and nobody could check it. Zero means no
grant — or, when Error is set, that we could not find out.

has_credit.description:
HasCredit reports that promo credit remains at this provider — so calls to it are
still being paid for with someone else's money.

is_paid_only.description:
IsPaidOnly reports the opposite: every call to this provider now costs real cash.
Exactly one of HasCredit and IsPaidOnly is true on a healthy row. BOTH false is
the deliberate "we could not tell" state, and it is reachable only with Error set.

provider.description:
Provider is the upstream we buy from, by its warehouse name ("do-ai", "openai").
The roster is the union of the seeded grants, DigitalOcean, and every provider the
usage ledger has burn for — so a provider appears once it has cost us anything.

remaining_cents.description:
RemainingCents is the grant still available, in USD cents, never negative. For
DigitalOcean it is the live negated account balance; for the rest it is grant minus
burn. Zero on a provider with no grant, and zero on one whose grant is spent —
HasCredit and IsPaidOnly separate those two.

runway_days.description: nil when burn is 0 / unknown (never a fabricated infinity)

data.description: Data is one row per provider, sorted by provider name.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A provider whose upstream read failed does not fail this
answer — it comes back as a row with `error` set, which is the whole reason that
field exists.

data.description: Data is the board. Null exactly when Status is "error".

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". An error here means the DigitalOcean account itself is
unreadable; a partial read still answers ok, with the failures named in
data.sources and the safety verdicts degraded via data.complete.

data.description:
Data is the page of records, newest first, and it is one of TWO shapes: this
store's own rows, or IAM's get-records payload forwarded verbatim by the fallback.
`integrity` being null is what tells you which — the fallback is a different trail.
Never null; an absent page is an empty list.

integrity.description:
Integrity is the live hash-chain verdict for THE ONE CHAIN these records came from,
carrying that chain's name so it cannot be read as the whole trail's. The trail is
a family of chains, one per process; GET /v1/admin/audit/verify answers for all of
them. NULL means no verdict, not a failed one: either the check could not run, or
these rows came from the IAM fallback, which has no chain of ours to verify.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A chain whose live verification failed still answers ok
— the verdict travels in `integrity`, and a verify problem must not hide the
records an auditor came for.

total.description:
Total is how many records match the filter across all pages, so a console can page
