without walking. Omitted on an error.

balanceCents.description:
BalanceCents is the prepaid wallet the org still holds, in USD cents. Money not yet
earned: it becomes revenue only as it is spent.

display.description: Display is the org's display name, falling back to the slug.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is the org's monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents, over the
subscriptions commerce counts as revenue. Contract value, not cash collected.

org.description: Org is the tenant slug — the row's identity.

plan.description:
Plan is the live subscription tier's name, or "pay-as-you-go" — which is also what
an org reads as when the subscriptions read failed, so it is not proof of no plan.

spendCents.description:
SpendCents is realized consumption over the trailing 30 days, in USD cents. The
table's primary sort, largest first.

arpuCents.description:
ARPUCents is TotalSpendCents divided by PayingCustomers, in USD cents — average
revenue per PAYING customer, not per signup. Zero when nobody pays, which is
division declining to happen rather than a measured zero.

customers.description: Customers is every org IAM lists, paying or not.

generatedAt.description: GeneratedAt is when the read ran, RFC3339. Nothing here is cached.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is fleet monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents — the sum of every org's
revenue-counting subscriptions. Orthogonal to TotalSpendCents, and never added to
it: one is contract value, the other is consumption.

payingCustomers.description:
PayingCustomers counts the orgs with spend or MRR above zero. It is the ARPU
denominator, chosen so a fleet of free signups cannot deflate the number.

perCustomer.description: PerCustomer is every org, richest first by 30-day spend, then by balance held.

sources.description:
Sources is the freshness strip: "iam" for the org directory, "commerce" for the
money, and "commerce-ledger" when the usage history behind SpendTrend was partial.
A not-ok commerce row means the totals above are an UNDERCOUNT, not a fleet that
earned less.

spendTrend.description:
SpendTrend is fleet consumption bucketed by DAY over the last 30 days, each point's
value in USD cents. The axis is continuous: a day with no usage is a real 0.

totalBalancesCents.description:
TotalBalancesCents is prepaid credit held across the fleet, in USD cents. A
LIABILITY, not revenue — it is money customers have not spent yet.

totalSpendCents.description:
TotalSpendCents is realized consumption across the fleet over the trailing 30 days,
in USD cents. This is the revenue figure; balances above are not.

data.description: Data is the board. Null exactly when Status is "error".

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". Only an unreadable IAM org directory is an error: a
per-org money failure degrades that row to zeros and marks the commerce source, so
the board still answers.

category.description:
Category is the plan's category as the subscription event declared it. Empty is a
real bucket — subscriptions whose plan carries no category land there.

mrrCents.description: MRRCents is this category's run-rate MRR, active subscriptions only.

subscriptions.description:
Subscriptions counts every non-canceled subscription in the category, trialing
included. So a category of nothing but trials shows subscriptions above zero and
mrrCents at zero, which is the honest reading.

category.description: Category is that plan's category. Empty for a pay-as-you-go org.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is the org's run-rate MRR, summed over its active subscriptions. Zero for
a pay-as-you-go org, which is a true zero and not a gap.

org.description: Org is the organization id, which is the row's identity.

plan.description:
Plan is the label of the org's LARGEST subscription by MRR, so an org on several
plans is named by the one it pays most for. An org with usage but no subscription
at all reads "pay-as-you-go".

seats.description: Seats is licensed seats across all the org's non-canceled subscriptions.

since.description:
Since is when the org's OLDEST live subscription began, RFC3339 — how long it has
been a customer. Omitted for an org that has never subscribed.

status.description:
Status is that subscription's state — `active`, `trialing`, `past_due`. A
pay-as-you-go org reads "active", since it is spending.

usageCents.description:
UsageCents is the org's metered spend over the window. It is the tiebreaker in the
ranking, and the only revenue a pay-as-you-go org has.

at.description: At is when the movement happened, RFC3339. The feed is ordered by it, newest first.

category.description:
Category is the plan's category at the moment of the movement — the same bucket
revenue.byCategory sums into.

mrrDeltaCents.description:
MRRDeltaCents is SIGNED: positive for a creation, negative for a cancellation. It
is the run-rate this one movement added or took away, so summing the feed over the
window gives revenue.netNewMrrCents.

org.description: Org is the organization whose subscription moved.

plan.description: Plan is the plan's human label at the moment of the movement.

type.description:
Type is `created` or `canceled` — the warehouse's event name normalised to the two
movements this feed carries.

active.description:
Active counts this plan's subscriptions in the `active` state — the ones MRRCents
is summed over.

category.description: Category is the plan's category, the same bucket revenue.byCategory sums into.

mrrCents.description: MRRCents is this plan's contribution to run-rate MRR, active subscriptions only.

name.description:
Name is the plan's human label, as the warehouse last saw it. A plan renamed
mid-life shows one of its names, not both.

plan.description: Plan is the plan's stable id — the key subscriptions are grouped by.

seats.description:
Seats is licensed seats across ALL of this plan's non-canceled subscriptions,
trialing included — a wider set than Active, so seats can be non-zero on a plan
carrying no MRR at all.

trialing.description: Trialing counts this plan's subscriptions still in a trial. Not yet revenue.

activeSubscriptions.description:
ActiveSubscriptions counts every non-canceled subscription — trialing and past_due
included. It is deliberately a wider set than the one MRRCents sums, so this can be
non-zero while MRR is zero.

arrCents.description:
ARRCents is MRRCents times twelve. A run-rate restatement of today's MRR, not a
forecast: nothing in it anticipates growth, churn or an annual discount.

byCategory.description:
ByCategory is the plan mix: run-rate MRR per plan category, largest first. It sums
to MRRCents. Never null.

churnedMrrCents.description:
ChurnedMRRCents is the MRR carried by subscriptions CANCELED inside the window,
reported as a POSITIVE magnitude — the sign convention lives in NetNewMRRCents,
which subtracts it, not here.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is run-rate monthly recurring revenue, in USD cents, summed over the
subscriptions whose LATEST lifecycle event left them `active`. Trialing, past_due
and unpaid subscriptions contribute nothing — the predicate is exactly commerce's
CountsTowardMRR, spelled in SQL because this board reads the warehouse rather than
calling the Go function.

netNewMrrCents.description:
NetNewMRRCents is NewMRRCents minus ChurnedMRRCents. Negative means the fleet lost
more recurring revenue than it won over the window. It counts only creations and
cancellations — an upgrade or downgrade in place moves MRRCents without appearing
here.

newMrrCents.description:
NewMRRCents is the MRR carried by subscriptions CREATED inside the window. Gross,
and positive.

payingCustomers.description:
PayingCustomers counts distinct ORGS with at least one active subscription carrying
MRR above zero. Orgs, not subscriptions: an org on three plans counts once.

trials.description:
Trials counts subscriptions currently in a trial. Revenue that has not started, so
it is reported beside MRR and never inside it.

byPlan.description:
ByPlan is every plan the fleet has a live subscription on, richest first by MRR.
Never null.

canceled.description:
Canceled is how many were canceled inside the window. Not a rate: divide by New, or
by activeSubscriptions, only if you mean to.

new.description: New is how many subscriptions were created inside the window.

recent.description:
Recent is the movement feed, newest first, capped at twenty and bounded by the same
window. It is a sample of what New and Canceled counted, not the whole of it.
Never null.

trialsActive.description:
TrialsActive is how many subscriptions are trialing right now. The same number as
revenue.trials, restated on the panel an operator works trials from.

instrumented.description:
Instrumented reports that at least one metered debit was observed in the window.
False means NOT MEASURED — the two fields below are then meaningless rather than
zero, and gaps says so. It is the difference between "nobody used the API" and
"nothing is emitting usage events yet".

requests.description: Requests is how many billed API calls the window recorded — one per debit event.

windowUsageCents.description:
WindowUsageCents is metered API spend over the window, in USD cents. Consumption
revenue, entirely separate from MRR — adding the two double-counts nothing but
invents a figure the business does not have.

count.description: Count is the node count to set.

id.description: ID is the DOKS cluster id, from the path.

pool.description:
Pool is the node pool, from the path. Its DO id or its name — both are unique
within a cluster, and an operator reads the name off the board.

t.description:
T is the bucket key, and its shape says which interval the series was built at:
"2006-01-02" for a day, the ISO week's Monday in the same form for a week,
"2006-01" for a month. Buckets are enumerated end to end over the window, so the
axis is continuous and successive points are one interval apart.

value.description:
Value is the bucket's total, in the unit its own series carries: CENTS for spend,
revenue and usage; a COUNT for signups, active customers, cumulative customers and
churn. A bucket nothing landed in is an honest 0, not a gap — the axis was
enumerated first and every bucket exists whether or not anything filled it.

description.description: Description is one line saying what the service is, for the board.

displayName.description:
DisplayName is the name the launch board shows. It also titles the switch
("Waitlist · <displayName>") the first time the service is registered.

hosts.description:
Hosts is every request host this service governs — "chat.hanzo.ai",
"hanzo.chat". Each is normalized (lowercased, port stripped) and the set
REPLACES the stored one, so an edit that omits a host stops governing it. A
host another service already claims is skipped: first claim wins.

service.description:
Service is the slug to onboard or edit, lowercased on the way in. Required.
It is the registry key and it names the switch — waitlist.<service> — so a
slug that already exists edits that service rather than creating a second.

waitlistMode.description:
WaitlistMode is the launch mode for a NEW service: true gates it to approved
users, false opens it. On a re-register it is IGNORED — the live switch is
preserved, so editing the hosts of an opened service never silently closes it.

WaitlistMode is the mode IN FORCE: true means the service is gated to
approved users, false means it is open to anyone. It is read from the
waitlist.<service> switch at the moment of the read, not stored on the
registry row, so it reflects a flip made anywhere in the fleet within one
evaluation TTL.

at.description:
At is when the scan ran, RFC3339 in UTC. Analyze takes it as an argument instead of
reading a clock, which is what makes the whole fold byte-reproducible in a test.

clusters.description:
Clusters is every DOKS cluster in the account, each with the rollup of its scan.
A cluster DO reports appears here even when its Kubernetes never answered.

complete.description:
Complete reports that EVERY cluster answered. It is the gate in front of every
destructive verdict on this board: while it is false nothing is deletable,
expandable or scalable, because the cluster that stayed silent is exactly the one
that might be holding the volume.

cost.description: Cost is what the fleet bills per month, in cents, plus what could be recovered.

findings.description:
Findings is the audit pass over everything above, sorted worst first: severity,
then money, then id. Empty means the fold found nothing worth a human's attention.

incompleteReason.description:
IncompleteReason names the clusters that did not answer and what their silence
costs, in the operator's language. Empty exactly when Complete is true, and it is
the same sentence every blocked row then repeats as its own BlockedReason.

loadBalancers.description:
LoadBalancers is every DO load balancer, attributed to a cluster by the Service
that claims it, or failing that by its member droplets.

nodes.description:
Nodes is EVERY droplet in the account, not only cluster members. A droplet no
cluster claims has an empty cluster and is the only kind this board will delete.

sources.description:
Sources is one freshness row per upstream read: `do.clusters`, `do.droplets`,
`do.volumes`, `do.loadBalancers`, and `k8s.<cluster name>` for each cluster scanned.
A row with ok=false is usually why Complete is false.

totals.description: Totals are the fleet counts — how many of each thing, and how much capacity.

volumes.description:
Volumes is every block-storage volume, each carrying the state machine's verdict
on who owns it. It is the list the safety rule exists for.

at.description:
At is when the aggregator ran, RFC3339. It is the READ's timestamp, shared by every
row in the list — not a per-source last-success time, so it never implies a stale
source is fresh.

error.description: Error is why the read failed, and is empty exactly when OK is true.

name.description:
Name identifies the upstream read, dotted by system: "do.volumes", "do.balance",
"k8s.hanzo-k8s", "iam.orgs", "billing.subscriptions". It is stable, so a console
can keep per-source state across reads.

ok.description:
OK is whether that read succeeded. False is the whole point of this row: an
aggregator answers with what it got rather than failing, so the only way a reader
can tell a real zero from a missing source is here.

rows.description:
Rows is how many records came back. Zero with ok=true is a genuine empty result;
zero with ok=false means nothing was read at all.

display.description:
Display is the same slug as Org. The warehouse holds no friendly name and this read
does no per-org IAM fan-out, so it repeats the slug rather than inventing one.

id.description:
ID is commerce's subscription id — the row's identity and the warehouse GROUP BY
key. One row per subscription, so an org on several plans has several rows.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is the subscription's monthly recurring revenue in USD cents — already
interval-normalized and multiplied by seats by the emitter, so an annual plan
reports a twelfth here and not its yearly price. Reported for EVERY row, including
trialing and canceled ones, which are not revenue: filter on Status before summing.

org.description: Org is the tenant that holds the subscription, and what ?org= matches exactly.

plan.description:
Plan is the plan's human label as of the subscription's latest event. A plan
renamed mid-life reports the name it carries now.

renews.description:
Renews is the current period's end, RFC3339 — when it next bills. On a canceled
subscription it is the last period's end, so it is a date in the past, not a
promise of a charge.

started.description:
Started is the earliest event on this subscription, RFC3339 — when it first
appeared in the warehouse. The tiebreaker in the ranking, newest first.

status.description:
Status is the EFFECTIVE lifecycle state: `canceled` when the latest event is a
cancel, whatever the last status snapshot said, otherwise that snapshot, defaulting
to `active`. Common values are `active`, `trialing`, `past_due`, `canceled`.

user.description:
User is the individual the subscription was created by, from the event's
distinct_id. Empty for one created by a machine rather than a person.

data.description:
Data is the matching subscriptions, highest MRR first, then newest, capped by
limit. Canceled subscriptions are included unless ?status= excludes them.

msg.description: Msg is the query failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A warehouse that is not connected answers ok with an
empty list and total 0 — the honest not-yet-wired state, not a fleet with no
subscribers.

total.description: Total is how many matched BEFORE limit truncated. Omitted on an error.

data.description: Data is the board. Null only when the caller was refused.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. An absent warehouse still
answers "ok" with the full inventory — the telemetry gap is reported in
data.sources.

category.description:
Category is the board's grouping: Launch, Signup, Subsystems, Gateway or
Network. Any subsystem may register a switch with a category of its own, so
treat it as a label to group by, not a fixed set.

description.description:
Description is what flipping this switch does, written by whoever registered
it — including the preconditions for flipping it, where there are any.

env.description:
Env is the environment variable that supplies the fallback. Present only on
the boot-time switches, where env IS the mechanism; a runtime switch carries
none on purpose, so that this surface is the one place its value comes from.

key.description:
Key is the registry key, which is also the flag key the engine evaluates and
the path segment a write addresses: snake_case for the seeded platform set
(waitlist_open, public_signup), waitlist.<service> for a launch gate.

label.description: Label is the switch's title on the board.

readOnly.description:
ReadOnly marks a switch the process reads once at BOOT (subsystem activation,
the network ids). Writing it is not refused and the stored value is real, but
the running process keeps its boot value until it is restarted — so a flip
here is a request for a redeploy rather than a hot change.

source.description:
Source is where Value came from, in the order they are tried: "flags" (a
stored definition — the only one a cockpit write produces), "env" (the Env
var below), or "default" (the registered literal). Anything but "flags"
means nothing has ever been written for this key.

type.description: Type is how Value is to be read back: bool, int or string.

value.description:
Value is the value IN FORCE right now, always as a string whatever Type says
— "true"/"false" for a bool, decimal digits for an int. It is what the
running deployment is using, not what is stored: an unstored switch reports
its env or literal fallback here.

attachedGiB.description: AttachedGiB is the provisioned capacity of the attached volumes, in GiB.

attachedVolumes.description: AttachedVolumes counts the volumes DO reports attached to a droplet right now.

clusters.description:
Clusters is how many DOKS clusters DigitalOcean reports, scanned or not. It is the
denominator the completeness gate counts unanswered clusters against.

detachedGiB.description:
DetachedGiB is the provisioned capacity of the detached volumes, in GiB. With
AttachedGiB it sums to VolumeGiB.

detachedVolumes.description:
DetachedVolumes is the exact complement of AttachedVolumes — bound, released and
unreferenced together, so the two always sum to Volumes. Detached is NOT idle and
NOT garbage: most of these are live data between mounts.

idlePVCs.description:
IdlePVCs counts volumes whose PVC is Bound but which no running pod mounts. A
review queue, never a delete queue — the usual member is a stopped database — and
deliberately excluded from ReclaimableMonthly.

loadBalancers.description: LoadBalancers is every DO load balancer in the account.

localDiskGiB.description:
LocalDiskGiB is the droplets' own disk, summed. Broken out precisely so it is never
added to VolumeGiB: it is included in each droplet's own monthly price and DO does
not bill it as block storage.

measuredGiB.description:
MeasuredGiB is the PROVISIONED capacity of the measured volumes — how much of the
fleet UsedGiB and WastedGiB were computed from, not how much of it is full.

measuredVolumes.description:
Fill. MeasuredVolumes/UnmeasuredVolumes are the honesty denominator: UsedGiB and
WastedGiB describe the measured set ONLY, so a board showing waste must show how
much of the fleet the figure was computed from. Unmeasured capacity contributes
nothing to either — it is not assumed empty, and it is not assumed full.

nodes.description:
Nodes is every droplet in the account, cluster member or not — the same population
as Snapshot.nodes, which is a superset of the machines Kubernetes knows about.

unmeasuredGiB.description:
UnmeasuredGiB is the provisioned capacity of the unmeasured volumes, in GiB — the
size of the blind spot behind UsedGiB and WastedGiB.

unmeasuredVolumes.description:
UnmeasuredVolumes counts volumes no kubelet reported a reading for. Not measured is
a different fact from empty, so these contribute to neither UsedGiB nor WastedGiB.

unreferencedGiB.description:
UnreferencedGiB is the provisioned capacity of the unreferenced volumes, in GiB —
the space a delete would hand back.

unreferencedVolumes.description:
UnreferencedVolumes counts the volumes no PV in any cluster names — the deletable
set, and the only one. It is a count of CANDIDATES: whether the button is live
still depends on Complete.

usedGiB.description:
UsedGiB is what the measured filesystems actually hold. Summed in BYTES and
converted once at the end, so hundreds of sub-GiB readings do not each round to
zero on the way in.

volumeGiB.description:
VolumeGiB is the PROVISIONED block-storage capacity, in whole GiB — the number
DigitalOcean bills for. It excludes droplet local disk entirely; see LocalDiskGiB.

volumes.description: Volumes is every block-storage volume in the account.

wastedGiB.description:
WastedGiB is provisioned minus measured across the measured set, in billed GiB. A
LOWER BOUND on fleet waste, and not the same money as ReclaimableMonthly: this
space sits inside volumes holding live data. See Cost.wastedMonthly.

broken.description: Broken counts the chains whose hash chain fails; each names where.

chains.description: Chains is every chain of the family, in name order.

intact.description: Intact counts the chains that verified end to end.

records.description:
Records is the total number of records walked across every chain that was
read. It counts nothing for an unread chain.

unread.description:
Unread counts the chains that could not be read. NOT a pass: nothing is known
about their contents.

data.description:
Data is one row per (provider, model) over the window, most expensive first. Never
null; empty also means the warehouse was unreachable, so read it beside the credit
ledger before concluding nothing was spent.

msg.description: Msg is the failure, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A warehouse that is not connected still answers ok with
an empty list — this is a dashboard read, and it degrades rather than refusing.

cost_cents.description:
CostCents is what those calls cost US at the provider, in USD cents. Upstream
spend, not what a customer was billed. The rows are ordered by it, largest first.

model.description: Model is the model those calls named, as the usage ledger recorded it.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the calls went to, joining this row to the credit ledger.

requests.description: Requests is how many calls the window recorded for this provider and model.

tokens.description:
Tokens is total tokens across the window's calls — prompt and completion together,
as the meter summed them.

amountCents.description:
Amount is the period's cost in USD cents, POSITIVE — money out is not negated
here. Summed across lines it is the platform COGS the margin subtracts.

note.description:
Note is commerce's own caveat on the line — usually how an estimate was reached.
Omitted when there is none.

service.description:
Service is what we pay them FOR, so one vendor can bill several lines. Commerce
chooses the vocabulary; this surface reports it verbatim.

vendor.description:
Name is who we pay — the vendor's own name ("digitalocean", "anthropic"). The wire
spells it `vendor`; a line is identified by this together with Service.

data.description:
Data is the verdict for every chain the deployment keeps — a set, because the trail
is a family of chains, one per process, and no single boolean is true of all of
them. Null exactly when Status is "error". A BROKEN or UNREAD chain is still an ok
answer: read the counts inside before concluding the trail is sound.

msg.description: Msg is why the walk could not run, and is empty on success.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". A deployment with no audit store is an ERROR here, not
an empty pass: "there is nothing to check" and "everything checks out" must never
render the same on a compliance surface.

blockedReason.description:
BlockedReason is why not, in the operator's language — which cluster's PV holds it,
or which clusters went unanswered. Empty exactly when Deletable is true.

cluster.description:
Cluster/ClusterID are the PROVEN owner — resolved through a PV that names this
volume, never through the tag.

clusterId.description:
ClusterID is that cluster's UUID. Falls back to the cluster of the droplet the
volume is physically attached to, which is evidence of the same quality: live
kernel state, not a label someone wrote once.

controller.description:
Controller is the workload owning the pod that mounts this volume
("StatefulSet/luxd"), or "" when nothing mounts it. It names who has to act.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when DO created the volume, RFC3339. Age is corroboration for a human
judging an orphan, never an input to the deletable verdict.

deletable.description:
Deletable is the standing verdict: this volume is unreferenced AND the scan was
complete enough to prove it. It is the only thing the delete route consults, and it
is recomputed from a fresh scan at the moment the button is pressed.

dropletIds.description:
DropletIDs are the droplets DO reports this volume attached to. Non-empty is hard
kernel-level evidence the volume is in use right now. Never null.

expandBlockedReason.description:
ExpandBlockedReason is why a grow is refused: a PV claims the volume but no PVC
does, so growing the device would leave the PV declaring a capacity that is wrong.
Empty exactly when Expandable is true.

expandable.description:
Expandable/ExpandBlockedReason are the GROW verdict, kept separate from Deletable
because the two ask opposite questions: a volume is deletable when nothing uses it,
and expandable when something uses it in a way this board can grow completely.

hasUsage.description:
HasUsage reports whether a kubelet actually MEASURED this volume's filesystem.

False means NOT MEASURED. It does NOT mean empty, and the three fields below are
meaningless — not zero — when it is false. A reading exists only while a running pod
has the volume mounted on a node that answered; a detached, idle or unreferenced
volume has none. Rendering an unmeasured volume as "0 used / 100% wasted" would
invent the single most expensive lie this board could tell, so every consumer must
branch on this flag and show unknown.

id.description:
ID is the DigitalOcean volume id. It is also the `spec.csi.volumeHandle` a
PersistentVolume names, which is what makes the cross-cluster liveness test an
exact match rather than a guess.

idle.description:
Idle is Bound with nothing mounting it: live data nobody is currently reading,
typically a stopped database. It is a queue for a human and is deliberately kept
out of Cost.reclaimableMonthly.

monthlyCents.description:
MonthlyCents is SizeGiB at DO's rate of 10 cents per GiB per month. It is charged
on provisioned capacity, so an empty volume and a full one of the same size cost
exactly the same.

mountedBy.description:
MountedBy lists the `namespace/name` of every running pod mounting this volume.
Empty on a Bound volume means idle — a review signal, never a delete signal.
Never null.

name.description:
Name is the DO volume name. DOKS-provisioned volumes are named `pvc-<uuid>`, which
is a naming convention and NOT evidence of ownership — only a PV reference is.

nodeName.description:
NodeName is the name of the first attached droplet, or "" when detached. Carried so
a refusal can name the machine an operator would have to go look at.

pv.description:
PV is the name of the PersistentVolume that claims this volume, or "" when no PV in
any scanned cluster does. Non-empty is the proof that makes it undeletable.

pvPhase.description:
PVPhase is that PV's phase — `Bound`, `Released`, `Available` or `Failed`. Bound
means live data; anything else means the claim is retired but the PV still exists,
so a human retires the PV before the volume can go.

pvcName.description:
PVCName is that claim's name. It plus the namespace is what the fill reading and
the mounting pods are keyed by, so an empty PVCName means neither can exist.

pvcNamespace.description: PVCNamespace is the namespace of the claim the PV is bound to, or "" when unbound.

region.description:
Region is DO's region slug ("nyc3"). A volume can only ever attach to a droplet in
its own region, so this bounds where it could possibly be in use.

sizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the PROVISIONED size — what DigitalOcean bills. It is not the
filesystem's capacity, which is a few percent smaller after format overhead.

state.description:
State is the ownership verdict, one of `attached`, `bound`, `released`,
`unreferenced`. The machine is total and ordered — attachment beats reference,
reference beats absence — and `unreferenced` is the ONLY deletable state.

tagCluster.description:
TagCluster is the `k8s:<uuid>` tag. ADVISORY ONLY: it outlives the cluster that
set it. Shown so the operator can see tag-vs-truth disagree, never acted on.

usedBytes.description:
UsedBytes is the measured filesystem usage. BYTES, not GiB: the volumes this exists
to catch hold a fraction of a GiB in 200, and rounding that to an integer GiB would
print the very 0 the flag above exists to prevent.

wastedGiB.description:
WastedGiB is provisioned minus measured, in the unit DigitalOcean BILLS: whole GiB
of the volume's own size, never the filesystem's capacity — a 200 GiB volume carries
a 196 GiB filesystem after format overhead, and the invoice says 200.

wastedMonthlyCents.description:
WastedMonthlyCents is WastedGiB at the same 10 cents per GiB per month. Money the
fleet pays for empty space inside a volume that is IN USE — so it is not
collectable by any button here, only by the copy-and-swap migration the matching
finding spells out. Zero when HasUsage is false, which means unknown, not none.

id.description: ID is the DO volume id, from the path.

name.description:
Name is the snapshot name on the snapshot action. Blank gets a deterministic
"<volume>-predelete-<unix>" so the undo is findable in the DO console.

sizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the target size on the resize action. A volume only ever grows —
ExpandTo is the verdict that refuses a shrink, so this is not validated here.

snapshot.description:
Snapshot is the snapshot-first switch on DELETE. Anything other than the literal
"false" snapshots before destroying — the snapshot IS the undo, so waiving it is
deliberate and explicit.

data.description:
Data is the snapshot DigitalOcean created — the undo, addressable in the DO
console. Null exactly when Status is "error", which means no snapshot exists.

msg.description: Msg is why the snapshot failed, and is empty on success.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error".

displayName.description:
DisplayName is the label to render. It carries the same value as Name today:
this answer is assembled from the sanitized identity headers, which carry no
separate display name.

email.description:
Email is the operator's email, and the actor an audited admin write is
recorded under.

isSuperAdmin.description:
IsSuperAdmin is the platform-sudo fact: true iff Owner is the reserved admin
org. That is IAM's IsSuperAdmin predicate and the ONE thing every
cross-tenant surface checks — an org's own isAdmin is a different power and
never grants it.

isWhiteLabel.description:
IsWhiteLabel marks the admitted NON-super tier: an admin of an enabled
white-label tenant org. Mutually exclusive with IsSuperAdmin (the gate lets
exactly one tier through). The operator SPA reads it to render the SUBTREE
cockpit — the fleet god-view nav (finance/revenue/metrics/o11y/providers) is
hidden — while a super sees the whole fleet.

name.description: Name is the IAM user name — the login handle, unique within Owner.

owner.description:
Owner is the IAM org this operator belongs to: the reserved admin org for a
SuperAdmin, the tenant's own slug for a white-label admin. It is read off the
validated principal the gate just checked, never from a client claim.

scopeOrgs.description:
ScopeOrgs is the caller's visible tenant window: empty for a SuperAdmin (means
ALL orgs), or the WL tenant's own subtree (today the singleton {org}). The SPA
threads it through the faceting/drill-down layer so a WL tenant can never widen
a filter past their subtree.

end.description:
End is the moment of this read, RFC 3339 UTC. The window is always right up
to now; there is no lag to allow for.

evalRuns.description:
EvalRuns is the twelve most RECENT eval runs, newest first — recency, not
quality.

evals.description: Evals is the eval plane's band: the trace half and the score half.

o11yAi.description:
O11yAI is the generation rollup over gen_ai spans. Its money is US DOLLARS,
unlike Usage below — the two halves of this board come from different planes
and each keeps its plane's unit.

o11yAiModels.description:
O11yAIModels is the twelve busiest models by GENERATION count, from gen_ai
spans. It answers the same question as TopModels from the other plane, and its
money is US dollars.

range.description:
Range is the window every figure below covers: 24h, 7d or 30d. It is the
NORMALIZED value — an unrecognized ?range reads as 30d and says so here.

scoreNames.description: ScoreNames is the twelve busiest scorers, each with its own distribution.

scoreSeries.description:
ScoreSeries is the average eval score bucketed over the window, oldest first.
This series IS the training/eval progress signal on this board.

start.description: Start is the window's lower bound, RFC 3339 UTC, derived from Range.

topActors.description:
TopActors is per-PRINCIPAL spend from the same ledger — whose bill it is,
which the per-model board cannot answer.

topModels.description:
TopModels is the twelve busiest models by request count, from the billing
ledger. Money in these rows is US cents.

usage.description:
Usage is the fleet LLM-usage band from the ledger the gateway writes. Its
money is US CENTS.

actor.description:
Actor is the principal the ledger recorded, "<org>/<sub>". A value naming
an IAM APPLICATION rather than a person means that spend has no human
owner — which is the row to read first.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost, in US cents, as the ledger recorded it.

requests.description: Requests is how many calls that principal made in the window.

tokens.description: Tokens is the total tokens those calls consumed.

avgScore.description:
AvgScore is the unweighted mean of every score value in the window,
regardless of scorer, to 4dp. Because the scorers are pooled it also moves
when the MIX of scorers changes, so read it as a trend and the per-scorer
rows for the level.

datasets.description: Datasets is how many distinct datasets those traces ran against.

latencyMsAvg.description:
LatencyMsAvg is the mean model-under-test call duration in milliseconds,
averaged only over traces whose end time is after their start — an unfinished
trace does not drag it down.

models.description: Models is how many distinct models were under test.

runs.description: Runs is how many DISTINCT eval runs left traces in the window.

scoreNames.description: ScoreNames is how many distinct scorers produced them.

scores.description:
Scores is how many individual score values were recorded, across every
scorer.

traces.description: Traces is how many eval traces were recorded — one per model-under-test call.

costUsd.description:
CostUsd is their summed cost in US DOLLARS — the span attribute's unit, not
the cents the ledger leaderboard beside this uses.

generations.description: Generations is how many gen_ai spans named it. The board ranks on this.

model.description:
Model is the model the span reported answering as, falling back to the model
it was asked for when the response named none.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost, in US cents.

model.description:
Model is the model id the ledger recorded. Unattributed rows carry no model
and are left out rather than ranked as a nameless one.

requests.description: Requests is how many calls went to it. The board ranks on this.

tokens.description: Tokens is what those calls consumed.

costUsd.description:
CostUsd is their summed cost in US DOLLARS, not cents: it is the span
attribute's native unit and is carried through unconverted.

generations.description:
Generations is how many LLM calls the fleet made in the window — one per
gen_ai span.

latencyMsAvg.description:
LatencyMsAvg is the mean generation duration in milliseconds, over spans that
recorded a duration at all.

latencyMsP95.description:
LatencyMsP95 is the 95th-percentile generation duration in milliseconds — the
tail a user actually feels.

avgValue.description: AvgValue is their mean, to 4dp, pooled across the run's scorers.

dataset.description:
Dataset is one dataset the run scored against — an arbitrary one of them if
the run spanned several, since a run is named per row here and a dataset is
not.

lastTs.description:
LastTs is when the run last recorded a score, RFC 3339 UTC. The board is
ordered by it, so these rows are the most RECENT runs, not the best ones.

runName.description:
RunName is the eval run's name, as the run recorded it. Unnamed runs are left
out.

scores.description: Scores is how many score values the run recorded in the window.

avgValue.description:
AvgValue is the mean of every score in that bucket, to 4dp. This series IS
the eval-progress signal.

count.description:
Count is how many scores the mean was taken over — the weight behind the
point, and what tells a real dip from a thin bucket.

ts.description:
Ts is the bucket's start, RFC 3339 UTC. The bucket width follows the range —
an hour at 24h, six hours at 7d, a day at 30d — so it is not a fixed unit.

count.description:
Count is how many values this scorer produced in the window. The board ranks
on this, so a busy scorer leads whether or not it scores well.

maxValue.description: MaxValue is the highest. With Min it bounds the spread the mean hides.

minValue.description: MinValue is the lowest single value this scorer recorded in the window.

name.description:
Name is the scorer's name. Its scale is the scorer's own — there is no fleet
convention that these are 0..1 — so compare a name against itself over time,
never one name against another.

completionTokens.description: CompletionTokens is the generated half of Tokens.

costCents.description:
CostCents is what those calls cost, in US CENTS — this half of the board is
the billing ledger, so it is cents while the gen_ai half is dollars.

models.description: Models is how many DISTINCT models were called, not a count of calls.

promptTokens.description: PromptTokens is the input half of Tokens.

requests.description:
Requests is how many calls the ledger recorded in the window, errored ones
included.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion across them.

data.description:
Data is the board. A warehouse that is not connected, or a table that is
missing, yields the ZERO board rather than a failure — so zeros here mean
either an idle fleet or a blind one, and this envelope cannot tell you which.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

activeCustomers.description:
ActiveCustomers is how many DISTINCT customers had at least one usage event
in each bucket. Empty when the ledger returned no usage at all.

arpuCents.description:
ARPUCents is average revenue per active customer over the window, in US
cents: window spend divided by MAU, falling back to TotalCustomers when
nothing was active. Integer division, so it truncates.

churn.description:
Churn is LOGO churn per month — customers active in the previous month and
not in this one. It counts customers, not revenue. The first point is always
zero because there is no month before it to compare against.

churnRatePct.description:
ChurnRatePct is churned customers as a percentage of the at-risk base,
pooled over the last SIX months rather than over Range.

computed.description:
Computed says which metrics on this board are backed by real data, keyed
growth, retention, active, churn, usage, revenue, mrr, arpu, ltv, nrr. False
means the number beside it is an honest zero because the ledger held nothing
to fold — NOT that it measured zero. Read it before reading any of them.

cumulativeCustomers.description:
CumulativeCustomers is the all-time customer count as of each bucket's END —
a running total, so it only rises and its last point is TotalCustomers.

dau.description:
DAU is how many distinct customers had a usage event in the last 24 hours. A
FIXED lookback — it ignores Range, so it does not change when the window
does.

generatedAt.description:
GeneratedAt is when this board was computed, RFC 3339 UTC. Nothing is
cached, so it is the moment of this request.

growthRatePct.description:
GrowthRatePct is the percentage change in signups against the immediately
preceding window of the same length; negative when signups fell. It is 0
when the prior window had none, which is not the same as flat.

interval.description:
Interval is the bucket width every series below uses: day, week or month,
derived from Range (7d and 30d give day, 90d gives week, all gives month).

ltvCents.description:
LTVCents is estimated lifetime value per customer, in US cents: ARPU divided
by the monthly churn rate. NULL until real churn is observed — with no churn
the formula divides by zero, and a huge number would read as good news.

mau.description:
MAU is the same over the last 30 days, and it is the denominator ARPUCents
uses.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is monthly recurring revenue as of NOW, in US cents, summed from
active subscriptions across the caller's window. Point-in-time: it is the
one revenue figure here that is not a fold of the usage window.

newCustomers.description: NewCustomers is how many of them signed up inside the window.

nrrPct.description:
NRRPct is net revenue retention. Always NULL: it needs a history of MRR over
time and commerce keeps only the current value, so there is nothing honest to
compute.

range.description:
Range is the requested window: 7d, 30d, 90d, or all (the last two years).
NORMALIZED — anything else reads as 30d and says so here.

retention.description:
Retention is the cohort triangle: signup month against months elapsed since,
as percentages of each cohort.

revenue.description:
Revenue is realized revenue per bucket, in US cents. For a pay-as-you-go
fleet it carries the same numbers as Usage; it is a separate field so a
console can theme the two differently.

signups.description:
Signups is new orgs created per bucket, from IAM's own createdTime. It is
the one series here that is always real: a signup timestamp exists whether
or not that tenant ever used anything.

sources.description:
Sources is one row per upstream this board read — iam and commerce-ledger —
with whether it answered and how many rows it gave. A ledger that answered
for only some orgs is marked degraded here, which is the only thing
distinguishing an undercount from a quiet month.

topCustomers.description:
TopCustomers is the ten biggest spenders in the window, largest first. A
customer with no spend is left out rather than listed at zero.

totalCustomers.description:
TotalCustomers is how many customers in the caller's window carry a signup
date at all, over ALL time rather than within Range.

usage.description: Usage is usage spend per bucket, in US cents, oldest first.

wau.description: WAU is the same over the last 7 days.

data.description: Data is the board. Null when Status is "error".

msg.description:
Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error" — here, that the tenant
window itself could not be resolved. A degraded upstream is not this: it is
reported in data.sources with Status still "ok".

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

hint.description:
Hint is the org slug behind Label, so two customers sharing a display name
stay distinguishable and a row can be clicked through to its tenant. Absent
when unknown.

label.description: Label is the customer's display name — what to render.

value.description: Value is that customer's spend over the window, in US cents.

created.description: Created is when the instance was created, as the engine reports it.

name.description: Name is the instance's name at the Base engine.

org.description:
Org is the tenant that owns the instance, and the key the scope filter runs
on. A row whose org is empty or outside the caller's subtree is DROPPED for
a non-SuperAdmin, so an instance the engine reports without an org is
visible only to a super.

plan.description: Plan is the plan the instance runs on, as the engine names it.

region.description: Region is where it is hosted, as the engine names it.

status.description:
Status is the engine's own lifecycle word for the instance — running and its
siblings. The vocabulary belongs to the Base engine, which is why this layer
forwards it rather than mapping it.

url.description: URL is where the instance is reached.

data.description:
Data is the instances in the caller's window, after the scope re-check. Null
when Status is "error".

msg.description:
Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error" (the engine was unreachable
or answered non-2xx). On a SUCCESS it may still carry an advisory: "the Base
engine is not yet embedded on this deployment" beside an empty list, which
is the honest not-yet state rather than a fleet with no instances.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. An unconfigured Base
engine answers "ok", not "error" — see Msg.

total.description:
Total is len(data): the caller's whole window after scope filtering,
unpaginated. Absent when the read failed.

id.description: ID is the cap to edit or remove, from the path. Unused by the list and create ops.

org.description:
Org is the tenant to act on. Required for a SuperAdmin — they must name their
target; ignored for a white-label admin, who always acts on their own org.

active.description:
Active is how many of them are still running — the ones whose LATEST
lifecycle event is not a terminal one (stop, destroy, terminate, delete,
off, shutdown, expire and their past tenses). Decided in the warehouse over
every machine, not over a page.

app.description: App is the application within that tenant, as the emitter recorded it.

kind.description:
Kind is the workload class: bot, machine, cluster, nodepool, container,
function and whatever else the emitter writes. An OPEN set, lowercased, not
an enum — a bot is a machine running the agent, a machine is raw compute —
so match it as a string and expect values this list does not have.

lastTs.description:
LastTs is the most recent event in the group, RFC 3339 UTC. For a group with
no active machines it is when the last one stopped.

machines.description:
Machines is how many DISTINCT machines of that kind ran in the window,
counted by machine id. Not a count of events.

org.description: Org is the tenant these workloads belong to.

project.description:
Project is the project within that app. With Org and App and Kind it forms
the group this row folds — the console's org to app to project tree is these
four columns.

spendCents.description:
SpendCents is what the group billed over the window, in US cents, summed
from the per-event prices.

data.description:
Data is one row per group, biggest spender first. Null when Status is
"error"; empty when there is genuinely nothing, or when the warehouse is
unavailable.

msg.description:
Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error" — the warehouse rejected
the query. A warehouse that is not connected, or a usage table not
provisioned yet, is a SUCCESS carrying an empty list instead.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description:
Total is len(data): the roll-up is one row per group, unpaginated. Absent
when the read failed.

mount.description: Mount is its filesystem path on the datastore node.

name.description: Name is the disk as the datastore names it.

pct.description:
Pct is UsedGiB as a percentage of SizeGiB, 0..100 to one decimal. The alert
thresholds read this.

sizeGiB.description: SizeGiB is its total capacity in GiB.

usedGiB.description:
UsedGiB is the space in use, in GiB to one decimal. This is the ONE real
fill on the board and the number to scale on.

ID.description:
ID is DigitalOcean's snapshot id. It is what a restore takes, so it is the handle
the undo actually hangs on — a delete that snapshotted first returns it.

Name.description:
Name is the snapshot's name, as given or as minted `<volume>-predelete-<unix>` when
the caller left it blank. It is how the snapshot is found in the DO console.

SizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the snapshot's size, from DO's size_gigabytes: the PROVISIONED size of
the volume it was taken from, not the bytes the snapshot occupies. DO bills
snapshots on used space, which this does not report.

data.description:
Data is the whole control-plane board — after the write, on a write, so a
caller sees the effect of its own flip without a second read. Null when the
op failed.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

data.description:
Data is IAM's own row array, forwarded byte-for-byte and therefore left
undescribed here: IAM's schema has one home, and a second copy of it in this
document would be free to drift from the one IAM serves. An absent page is
[], never null.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description: Total is IAM's count across all pages. Absent when the read failed.

data.description:
Data is the caller's own identity and tenant window. Null when Status is
"error".

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error". An error here is still HTTP 200 — the transport
reads this field, not the status line.

byOrg.description:
ByOrg is one line per customer, biggest spender first. The row SET comes
from revenue, so an org that was granted credit but no longer exists in IAM
is inside the fleet totals above and has no line of its own.

credits.description:
Credits is the granted-against-consumed ledger, including the balance
customers still hold.

generatedAt.description:
GeneratedAt is when the board was assembled, RFC 3339 UTC. Nothing here is
cached.

infrastructure.description:
Infra is what the platform costs to run: vendor COGS, the DigitalOcean
burn-down, and the reserve backing the payout programs.

margin.description:
Margin is revenue against cost, carried through from the finance board
unchanged so the two can never report different margins.

revenue.description:
Revenue is what customers actually pay: realized consumption, recurring
contract value, and the counts behind them.

sources.description:
Sources is one row per upstream, each name prefixed by the domain that read
it (revenue:, finance:, grants:audit, treasury) — a bare "commerce" appears
under two domains and would otherwise collide. A not-ok row means the total
it feeds is an UNDERCOUNT, not a smaller number.

consumedCents.description:
ConsumedCents is realized spend, in US cents. A credit is consumed exactly
when it is spent, so this is the same number revenue reports, stated once
from one source.

grantedCents.description:
GrantedCents is every credit successfully issued, in US cents, over the
whole grant history rather than a window. Refused grants are excluded — they
moved nothing.

grantedPrepaidCents.description:
GrantedPrepaidCents is the half backed by real money the customer paid in, in
US cents. With GrantedTrialCents it sums to GrantedCents.

grantedTrialCents.description:
GrantedTrialCents is the non-cash half — comps and promos we gave away — in
US cents. A grant whose source the ledger did not record counts here, since a
grant nobody paid for is the safer assumption.

grants.description:
Grants is how many successful grants make up GrantedCents. If it reaches the
scan bound the grants source is marked partial rather than the sum being
presented as complete.

outstandingCents.description:
OutstandingCents is the LIABILITY: prepaid and promo balance customers still
hold and have not burned. It is not revenue, and it is not GrantedCents
minus ConsumedCents — customers also add their own money.

doAvgDailyBurnCents.description:
DOAvgDailyBurnCents is the average DigitalOcean spend per day, in US cents.
Dividing the credit above by it is the runway.

doCreditRemainingCents.description:
DOCreditRemainingCents is the promo credit left on the DigitalOcean account,
in US cents — what is left to spend, not what was granted.

doMonthToDateCents.description: DOMonthToDateCents is DigitalOcean spend so far this month, in US cents.

period.description:
Period is the billing month the vendor COGS covers, "2006-01", as commerce
reports it. It bounds VendorCogsCents only — the DigitalOcean figures below
are month-to-date and the reserve is point-in-time.

treasuryReserveCents.description:
TreasuryReserveCents is the platform reserve backing the payout programs, in
US cents, read live from the treasury app. Zero here can mean an empty
reserve OR an unreachable treasury — the treasury row in sources is what
tells them apart.

vendorCogsCents.description:
VendorCogsCents is what the platform owes its vendors for Period, in US
cents, POSITIVE — money out is not negated. This is the COGS the margin
subtracts.

vendors.description:
Vendors is the COGS broken out per vendor and service line for Period, each
amount positive.

grossCents.description:
GrossCents is realized revenue minus vendor COGS, in US cents. Negative
means the fleet spent more on vendors than its customers consumed. GROSS
only: salaries, tooling and everything outside vendor COGS are not in it.

grossPct.description:
GrossPct is that margin as a percentage of revenue — 42.5 means 42.5%, not
0.425. Zero when revenue is zero, which is arithmetic rather than a claim of
break-even.

profitable.description:
Profitable is revenue strictly greater than COGS — the sign of GrossCents
stated outright, so no consumer has to decide what zero means.

runwayDays.description:
RunwayDays is DigitalOcean promo credit divided by average daily burn: how
long the credit lasts at today's rate, and nothing to do with the margin
above. NULL — never a large number — when DigitalOcean is unconfigured or
burn is zero, because no honest projection exists and an infinity would read
as safety.

balanceCents.description:
BalanceCents is the prepaid wallet the tenant still holds, in US cents —
money not yet earned.

display.description: Display is the org's display name, falling back to the slug.

grantedCents.description:
GrantedCents is credit successfully granted TO this tenant, in US cents,
across all history. Zero for a tenant that was never granted any.

grants.description: Grants is how many grants that was.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is the tenant's monthly recurring revenue, in US cents. Contract
value, not cash collected.

org.description: Org is the tenant slug — the row's identity.

plan.description:
Plan is the live subscription tier's name, or "pay-as-you-go" — which is
also what an org reads as when the subscriptions read failed, so it is not
proof of no plan.

spendCents.description:
SpendCents is realized consumption over the trailing 30 days, in US cents.
The board sorts on it, largest first.

arpuCents.description:
ARPUCents is realized spend divided by PAYING customers, in US cents — per
paying customer, not per signup, so free signups cannot deflate it.

arrCents.description:
ARRCents is MRRCents times twelve, in US cents. A projection of today's
contracts, not a measurement of a year.

customers.description: Customers is every org IAM lists, paying or not.

mrrCents.description:
MRRCents is fleet monthly recurring revenue, in US cents — contract value
from subscriptions. Orthogonal to RealizedCents and never added to it.

paying.description:
Paying is how many of them have spend or MRR above zero. It is the ARPU
denominator.

realizedCents.description:
RealizedCents is credit customers have actually CONSUMED, fleet-wide, in US
cents. This is the revenue figure — MRR beside it is contract value and the
two are never added.

end.description: End is the moment of this read, RFC 3339 UTC.

llm.description:
LLM is the generation rollup over gen_ai spans. Its money is US DOLLARS,
unlike Totals above — the two come from different planes and each keeps its
plane's unit.

logSeries.description: LogSeries is log volume over the SAME buckets as Series, so the two line up.

range.description:
Range is the window every figure below covers: 24h, 7d or 30d. It is the
NORMALIZED value — an unrecognized ?range reads as 30d and says so here.

series.description:
Series is usage bucketed over the window, oldest first. A bucket with no
traffic has no point — the series is not padded to a fixed length.

start.description: Start is the window's lower bound, RFC 3339 UTC, derived from Range.

topModels.description: TopModels is the ten busiest models by request count.

topOrgs.description: TopOrgs is the ten busiest tenants by request count.

topServices.description: TopServices is the twelve busiest services by trace count.

totals.description: Totals is the KPI band: the usage half, the trace half and log volume.

costUsd.description:
CostUsd is their summed cost in US DOLLARS, not cents: the span attribute's
native unit, carried through unconverted.

generations.description:
Generations is how many LLM calls the fleet made in the window — one per
gen_ai span. It counts the same activity the usage totals do, from the trace
plane instead of the billing ledger, so the two need not match exactly.

count.description: Count is the log lines emitted in that bucket, fleet-wide.

ts.description:
Ts is the bucket's start, RFC 3339 UTC, on the same buckets as the usage
series so the two can be read together.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost, in US cents.

model.description:
Model is the model id the ledger recorded. Unattributed rows carry no model
and are left out rather than ranked as a nameless one.

requests.description: Requests is how many calls went to it. The board ranks on this.

tokens.description: Tokens is what those calls consumed.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost, in US cents.

org.description: Org is the tenant slug.

requests.description:
Requests is how many calls that tenant made. The board ranks on this, so the
top rows are the busiest tenants and not necessarily the costliest.

tokens.description: Tokens is what those calls consumed.

data.description:
Data is the board. A warehouse that is not connected, or a table that is
missing, yields the ZERO board rather than a failure — so zeros here mean
either a quiet fleet or a blind one, and this envelope cannot tell you
which.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost, in US cents.

errors.description: Errors is how many of them failed.

requests.description: Requests is the calls served in that bucket.

tokens.description: Tokens is the tokens they consumed.

ts.description:
Ts is the bucket's start, RFC 3339 UTC. The width follows the range — an
hour at 24h, six hours at 7d, a day at 30d — so it is not a fixed unit.

latencyP95Ms.description:
LatencyP95Ms is that service's 95th-percentile span duration in
milliseconds.

requests.description:
Requests is how many spans it emitted in the window. The board ranks on
this.

service.description:
Service is the emitting service's name, from the span's own service column.
The whole cloud binary reports under ONE such name however many subsystems
it mounts, which is what the per-subsystem board next door exists to split
apart.

completionTokens.description: CompletionTokens is the generated half of Tokens.

costCents.description:
CostCents is what those calls cost, in US CENTS. The trace and gen_ai
figures elsewhere on this board are not in cents; this one is.

errors.description: Errors is how many of Requests the ledger marked failed.

latencyP50Ms.description:
LatencyP50Ms is the median request duration in milliseconds, over spans
rather than over ledger rows — so it covers every traced request, not only
the LLM ones counted above.

latencyP95Ms.description: LatencyP95Ms is the 95th percentile of the same durations.

latencyP99Ms.description: LatencyP99Ms is the 99th percentile — the tail worth paging on.

logVolume.description:
LogVolume is how many log lines the fleet emitted in the window. Volume only
— nothing here says how many of them were errors.

models.description: Models is how many distinct models were called.

orgs.description:
Orgs is how many DISTINCT tenants appear in the window — the fleet's active
tenant count, not a count of calls.

promptTokens.description: PromptTokens is the input half of Tokens.

requests.description:
Requests is how many LLM calls the fleet served in the window, across every
tenant, errored ones included. From the billing ledger.

services.description: Services is how many distinct services emitted a span in the window.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion tokens across those calls.

traceCount.description:
TraceCount is how many spans the fleet emitted in the window, across every
service. It counts TRACED REQUESTS, so it is a much larger number than
Requests above and is not a superset of it: one is the trace plane, the other
the billing ledger.

created.description: Created is when the account was created, as IAM records it (RFC 3339).

displayName.description: DisplayName is the human name IAM holds. Often empty; render Name when it is.

email.description: Email is the user's email address.

forbidden.description:
Forbidden is true when IAM has the account blocked: it exists and cannot sign
in. Distinct from deleted, which simply would not appear here.

isAdmin.description:
IsAdmin is admin OF THEIR OWN ORG — they manage that org's users and apps. It
is not platform privilege and grants nothing outside Owner.

isSuperAdmin.description:
IsSuperAdmin is platform sudo: true iff Owner is the reserved admin org. It is
derived here from Owner, which is the one predicate — never read off the user
row, so a tenant cannot set it on themselves.

lastSignin.description:
LastSignin is the last successful sign-in, as IAM records it. Empty for an
account that has never signed in — which is what an unused invite looks like.

name.description: Name is the IAM user name — the login handle, unique within Owner.

owner.description:
Owner is the org this user belongs to. A user belongs to exactly one, so this
is also the tenant column of the directory.

tag.description: Tag is IAM's free-form label on the user. Empty unless the tenant uses it.

created.description: Created is when the org was created, as IAM records it (RFC 3339).

creditsCents.description:
CreditsCents is the credit balance the tenant still holds, in US cents, from
the commerce wallet. What they have left, not what they were given.

display.description:
Display is the org's display name, falling back to the slug when IAM holds
none, so it is always renderable.

org.description: Org is the tenant slug — the key every other admin read joins on.

products.description:
Products is always 0. The fleet workload registry is not attributed to
tenants yet, and a count of the platform's own workloads on a tenant row
would be a number about somebody else.

spendCents.description:
SpendCents is the tenant's AI spend over the trailing 30 days, in US cents,
from the usage ledger. A tenant with no rows in that window reads a true zero.

tokens.description: Tokens is the tokens served for this tenant over that same 30-day window.

users.description: Users is the tenant's member count, from IAM's own total.

data.description:
Data is one row per tenant, sorted by slug. Null when the read failed, [] when
the caller's window is genuinely empty.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description:
Total is the whole directory's row count BEFORE paging, so a console can page
against it. Absent when the read failed, since there is then nothing to count.

activeProducts.description:
ActiveProducts is how many of those the operator reconciled to green health.
The gap against Products is everything not green, unknown health included.

creditsCents.description:
CreditsCents is the credit balance customers still HOLD — the liability, in
US cents, summed over the window from the commerce wallet. It is not revenue
and not spend.

drift.description:
Drift is how many workloads the operator flagged as drifting — its declared
image and what is actually running disagree. It counts the operator's own
verdict; this layer does not re-derive it.

lastSync.description:
LastSync is when this answer was assembled, RFC 3339 UTC. admin caches
nothing — the read IS the sync — so it is the time of this request and never
of an earlier batch.

orgs.description:
Orgs is how many tenants are in the caller's window: every org for a
SuperAdmin, their own subtree for a white-label admin.

products.description:
Products is how many workloads the operator is observing across the platform
namespaces — one per App CR.

sources.description:
Sources is one row per upstream this board fanned out to — iam, commerce,
usage, o11y, fleet — saying whether it answered, with how many rows, and why
not. It is what tells a zero above apart from a silence.

spendCents30d.description:
SpendCents30d is AI spend over the trailing 30 days, in US cents, folded from
the usage ledger (one row per served request).

tokens30d.description: Tokens30d is total tokens served over that same 30-day window.

users.description:
Users is the member count summed over those orgs. An org whose IAM read
failed contributes zero rather than failing the tile.

data.description: Data is the tile board. Null only when the caller was refused outright.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. This board answers "ok"
even when upstreams are down — a tile board that fails whole because one
source is unreachable is useless — so a degraded read is reported in
data.sources, not here.

declaredTag.description: spec.image.tag on the App CR (declared truth)

latestTag.description: newest released tag (GH release reader — empty until wired)

name.description:
Name is the operator App CR's name — the handle the operator, the PaaS board
and this one all address the workload by. Unique within its namespace.

org.description: image namespace (hanzoai|luxfi|docker.io/…)

updated.description:
Updated is always empty. The App CR carries no per-row reconcile timestamp and
this observation is taken live, so there is no moment to report; the time that
applies to the whole answer is the overview's lastSync.

data.description: Data is the matching workload rows. Null when the read failed.

msg.description:
Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error" — here, that the PaaS plane
could not be reached at all. A plane that answers with nothing observed yet is
a success carrying an empty list, which is a different fact.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description:
Total is len(data): the registry is the whole observed fleet after filtering,
unpaginated. Absent when the read failed.

active.description: Active is the master switch: false parks the offer without deleting it.

end.description: End is when the offer closes (RFC3339).

plans.description: Plans are the plan ids the offer applies to.

start.description: Start is when the offer opens (RFC3339).

data.description:
Data is the upstream's payload verbatim, left undescribed for the same reason
as iamRowsOut: re-describing someone else's schema here would be a second copy
of it, free to drift.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. It is THIS layer's verdict
on the forwarding; an upstream that answered carries its own status inside
data.

total.description:
Total is the upstream's row count when it forwarded a list, and absent when it
forwarded a single object — which is why it is optional rather than zero.

cohort.description:
Cohort is the signup month, YYYY-MM. Every customer who signed up in it is
in this row.

size.description:
Size is how many customers signed up in that month — the denominator behind
every percentage in Values.

values.description:
Values is the percentage of the cohort ACTIVE in each month after signup,
0..100, with values[0] the signup month itself. Its length varies by row: an
older cohort has more months behind it, which is what makes the grid a
triangle.

cohorts.description:
Cohorts is one row per signup month, oldest first, capped at the last
twelve. A month in which nobody signed up is omitted rather than shown
empty.

interval.description:
Interval is the cohort width, always "month": the triangle is built from
signup months and active months, and no other bucketing is offered.

periods.description:
Periods is the longest Values length across the cohorts — the width of the
triangle, so a renderer can size the grid before walking it.

services.description: Services is every registered service with its live waitlist mode.

service.description: Service is the slug to flip, taken from the path.

waitlistMode.description:
WaitlistMode is the new mode: true gates the service behind the waitlist, false
opens it. This is the launch lever.

service.description: Service is the row as it stands after the write, live mode included.

data.description:
Data is the one service the write touched, re-read after the write, so a
caller sees the effect of its own change without a second request. Null when
the write failed.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

data.description: Data is the launch board. Null when the read failed.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

active.description: Active is the switch itself: true enables the flag for every evaluation.

filters.description:
Filters is the optional rollout/payload block of a VALUED switch, e.g.
{"groups":[{"properties":[],"rollout_percentage":100}],"payloads":{"true":250}}.

key.description: Key is the switch to write, taken from the path (e.g. "waitlist.chat").

level.description:
Level is "warn" from 80% and "critical" from 90%. Below 80 no alert is
emitted at all — there is no third level meaning fine.

pct.description: Pct is the fill that raised the alert, 0..100.

volume.description:
Volume is the volume the alert is about. Only the datastore carries a
measured fill today, so it is the only name that appears here.

count.description:
Count is how many volumes the DigitalOcean account holds. A measurement only
when the snapshot is complete — otherwise it is zero because nothing was
read.

monthlyUsd.description:
MonthlyUsd is the fleet's block-storage cost in whole US DOLLARS per month —
capacity times DO's $0.10/GiB list price, rounded. A list-price estimate for
the ops budget, not an invoice line, and dollars rather than the cents the
money boards use.

pct.description: Pct is null, for the same reason as UsedGiB.

totalGiB.description: TotalGiB is their summed provisioned capacity in GiB.

usedGiB.description:
UsedGiB is null: with no per-volume fill there is no honest fleet total to
sum.

alerts.description:
Alerts is the near-full warnings, derived from the datastore fill. Empty
means nothing is near full AND also that there was no fill to judge —
Datastore being null is what tells those apart.

complete.description:
Complete is whether the fleet roll-up may be read as a MEASUREMENT. False
means DigitalOcean was not read, so the count, capacity and cost below are
unknown rather than zero — and zero is exactly what an account with no
volumes looks like, which is why the distinction has to travel beside them.

datastore.description:
Datastore is the analytics datastore's own volume, the one card carrying a
measured fill. NULL when the datastore is not connected or reported no
capacity — no card at all rather than a fabricated 0%.

fleet.description: Fleet is the DigitalOcean roll-up: count, capacity and monthly list cost.

incompleteReason.description:
IncompleteReason says which read did not happen and what that makes the
numbers, in a sentence fit to show an operator. Empty when Complete is true.

sources.description:
Sources is one row per upstream — do.volumes — with whether it answered, how
many rows it gave, and why not.

volumes.description:
Volumes is one row per DigitalOcean volume: capacity, region and attachment,
with fill absent.

attached.description:
Attached is whether at least one droplet has the volume mounted. A detached
volume still bills its full size, which is what makes this the reclaim
signal.

id.description: ID is DigitalOcean's own volume id.

name.description: Name is the volume's name at DigitalOcean.

pct.description:
Pct is null on every row, for the same reason as UsedGiB. The console
renders an em dash rather than a number nobody took.

region.description:
Region is the DO region slug it lives in (nyc3, sfo3). A volume can only
attach to a droplet in its own region.

service.description:
Service names the workload this volume backs. Empty on every row today:
nothing tags a DO volume with its consumer, and guessing one from the name
would be a claim rather than a reading.

sizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the PROVISIONED capacity in GiB. It is what is billed, attached
or not, used or not.

usedGiB.description:
UsedGiB is null on every row. DigitalOcean exposes capacity and attachment
but not fill, so nothing here has measured it — null means unmeasured, and
is not 0.

end.description: End is the moment of this read, RFC 3339 UTC.

range.description:
Range is the telemetry window the RED columns cover: 24h, 7d or 30d,
normalized the same way the o11y board normalizes it. It does NOT bound the
inventory — a subsystem appears whether or not it served anything.

rows.description:
Rows is one row per subsystem MOUNTED IN THIS PROCESS, in the composition
root's order. The row set comes from the mount index, not from the
warehouse, so a subsystem that served nothing appears as a real zero instead
of vanishing.

sources.description:
Sources is one row per input: mount-index (always ok — it IS this process),
traces, and trace-errors. The last two go not-ok when the warehouse is
absent, which is what says "telemetry unavailable" instead of implying every
subsystem served nothing.

start.description: Start is that window's lower bound, RFC 3339 UTC.

totals.description: Totals is the KPI band above the table.

enabled.description:
Enabled is whether it is switched ON in this process. Process-local and
always truthful — it needs no warehouse — which is what answers "is that row
empty because it is broken or because it is off".

errors.description: Errors is how many of those requests errored.

lastErrorAt.description:
LastErrorAt is when this subsystem last errored in the window, RFC 3339 UTC.
Empty when it did not — or when the last-error read failed, which the
trace-errors source reports.

lastErrorMessage.description:
LastErrorMessage is the span's status message. Empty when the span recorded
none, which is common: a span can be marked errored without a message.

lastErrorRoute.description:
LastErrorRoute is the route pattern that error was on, e.g. /v1/admin/orgs.
Empty when the span carried none.

lastErrorStatus.description:
LastErrorStatus is the HTTP status code it answered, as a STRING — it is a
span attribute, and attribute values arrive as text.

latencyP50Ms.description: LatencyP50Ms is its median request duration in milliseconds.

latencyP95Ms.description: LatencyP95Ms is its 95th percentile in milliseconds.

latencyP99Ms.description: LatencyP99Ms is its 99th percentile in milliseconds.

name.description:
Name is the subsystem's name in the mount index, and the label the request
span is stamped with. It is the join key between the inventory and the
warehouse: a warehouse row naming something this binary does not mount is
dropped rather than shown.

prefixes.description:
Prefixes is the route prefixes it answers on, e.g. /v1/admin. Always a list,
never null — empty means it mounts no HTTP routes of its own.

requests.description:
Requests is the traced requests it served in the window. Zero when the
warehouse is unavailable, so read the board's sources before reading it as
idle.

requestsPerMin.description:
RequestsPerMin is Requests averaged over the WHOLE window, to 2dp — a flat
mean, so a burst and a steady trickle of the same volume look alike here.

disabled.description: Disabled is the rest. With Enabled it sums to Subsystems.

enabled.description: Enabled is how many of them are switched ON.

errors.description: Errors is how many of them errored.

reporting.description: enabled AND served ≥1 traced request in the window

requests.description:
Requests is the traced requests every subsystem served in the window,
summed.

subsystems.description: Subsystems is how many are mounted in this binary — the row count.

data.description: Data is the acknowledgement. Null when the caller was refused.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

started.description:
Started is always true on a successful call. There is nothing to poll and
nothing to cancel: the next read is the refresh.

model.description:
Model is the model id the ledger recorded. Rows the ledger left unattributed
are dropped rather than rendered as a nameless slice.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is this model's share of the window's cost, in US cents.

tokens.description: Tokens is this model's share of the tokens.

byModel.description:
ByModel is the window split by model, busiest first, capped at the top ten so
the ranking stays honest without paying for a tail nothing draws.

series.description:
Series is that window bucketed by day, oldest first. A day with no traffic has
no point — the series is not padded.

totals.description: Totals is the whole window folded into one row.

data.description:
Data is the usage roll-up. A warehouse that is not connected yields zeros
here, not null — which reads as an idle fleet, so use the overview's
sources[] to tell the two apart.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

date.description:
Date is the bucket's calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. A day, not an instant:
the bucket covers the whole of it.

requests.description: Requests is that day's served-request count.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is that day's cost, in US cents.

tokens.description: Tokens is that day's token count.

requests.description:
Requests is how many were served — including the ones that errored, which
still consumed the call.

spendCents.description: SpendCents is what those requests cost, in US cents.

tokens.description: Tokens is prompt plus completion tokens across them.

data.description: Data is ONE page of users. Null when the read failed.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description: Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way.

total.description:
Total is IAM's count across ALL pages, not len(data) — it is what the console
pages against. Absent when the read failed.

data.description: Data is the board. Null only when the caller was refused.

msg.description: Msg is the failure reason when Status is "error", empty otherwise.

status.description:
Status is "ok" or "error", at HTTP 200 either way. A DigitalOcean outage
still answers "ok": an operator reads this board DURING an incident, and the
gap is named in data.incompleteReason rather than replacing the page.

email.description: Email identifies the entry to boost. Either this or RefCode is required.

points.description:
Points is how many points to award. Must be positive — this seam exists to move
someone UP toward the cutoff.

reason.description:
Reason is the operator's justification. Not sent to the engine; it is recorded on
the audit row, which is the point of asking for it.

refCode.description: RefCode identifies the entry by its referral code, when the email is unknown.

waitlist.description: Waitlist is the waitlist slug the grant lands on. Required.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
